docs.title: SIEVE: Scientific Evidence Evaluation & Verification Environment
docs.text:
SIEVE records why Mondo believes a claim, and packages that "why" so a curator, or a machine, can check it. It is an evidence model for ontology claims (subclass placements, mappings, synonyms, definitions, gene-disease attributes), defined as a profile of the SEPIO core information model and traced requirement by requirement to the Mondo requirements collection.

New here? Start with the Primer.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
Everything hangs off one container per claim, the versioned EvidencePacket:

  • A statement: the claim, as one of ten claim types (SubclassStatement, MappingStatement, SynonymStatement, ...). Subject, predicate and object sit on the statement; negated: true makes a negative claim.
  • Evidence items: the information used as evidence (ExternalRecord, prior claims (claim-type statements), TextPassage, Publication, WebPage, GuidelineDocument, ComputationalScore), in typed lists on the packet.
  • Evidence lines: each SieveEvidenceLine is one judgement that some items support or dispute the claim, with a strength in [0, 1] and the InterpretationActivity that produced it.
  • Assertion decisions: each AssertionDecision records whether the claim was accepted, rejected, kept as controversial or deferred, by whom, by which route, and on which packet version and inclusion score.

Two levels of judgement, three axes

Interpreting evidence (lines) and deciding on the claim (decisions) are recorded separately. Provenance (where a claim came from), evidence (whether it is supported) and data quality (whether the evidence was read correctly) are kept apart. The claim type's aggregation rule turns the lines into an inclusion score S in [-1, 1].

For every field, see the Data Model. For which requirement each part answers, see Requirements Traceability. The small, separate kernel for other Monarch projects is described in Minimal Evidence Model.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
uv sync --group dev

# Validate a packet against the profile
uv run linkml-validate -s schema/sieve.yaml -C EvidencePacket my_packet.yaml

# Regenerate the Pydantic model and the traceability page after schema edits
just gen-pydantic
just gen-traceability

# Run the profile, traceability and example tests
uv run pytest tests/test_profile_schema.py tests/test_profile_examples.py \
    tests/test_profile_checks.py tests/test_traceability.py

linkml-validate needs dates quoted in YAML (see Data Model). The fixtures in tests/data/profile/valid/ leave dates unquoted, so the CLI rejects them as they are; the tests load them with dates kept as strings.

Application layer not yet migrated

The review app, the DuckDB store, ingest, RDF export, scoring and the sieve CLI still target the pre-profile model and do not work with the current schema. They are being migrated (issues/issue_migrate_app_to_profile.md). The CLI Reference, Workflows and Python API pages mark which parts this affects.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
• Evidence-based curation of Mondo claims
  • Keeping the origin of a claim apart from the evidence for it
  • Mapping and cross-ontology alignment review
  • Policy-based and batch acceptance with an audit trail
  • Recording AI-extracted evidence with the checks a reviewer needs

docs.title: Authoring Packets as an AI Agent
docs.text:
This page is for AI agents (LLMs, autonomous pipelines) that produce evidence for SIEVE. It covers only the AI-specific parts: what an agent records, and which checks it must report honestly.

It does not re-teach the data model. Read these first:

  • SIEVE in Plain Terms: claims, items, lines, decisions.
  • Data Model: every class and field.

docs.title: What you produce
docs.text:
An agent's output is one EvidencePacket per claim, in the profile shape (camelCase, id and type on every entity). An agent typically contributes three things:

  • evidence items it created: a TextPassage with the verbatim quote it extracted, plus the Publication / WebPage / GuidelineDocument it came from;
  • evidence lines: its interpretation of those items, each with an InterpretationActivity of method_type: LLM_JUDGEMENT;
  • groundings: ResolutionChains recording how mentions in the passage were resolved to Mondo, HGNC or other ids, step by step.

An agent does not write assertion_decisions and does not set the inclusion score. Decisions are made by a person, or by a policy runner acting under a human-approved DecisionPolicy. Leave review_state: NOT_VERIFIED, and set proposing_channel: AI_AGENT when the agent proposed the claim.

docs.title: What the profile asks of AI evidence
docs.text:
Where Field What to record TextPassage statement_text The quote, verbatim. reported_in, document_version, text_location Which document and version, and where (section, character offsets). quote_verification VERIFIED only if a machine check found the quote in the source; otherwise NOT_CHECKED or FAILED. contributions The extraction act: contributor, role: EXTRACTOR, date, specified_by (prompt or workflow version), run_id. Required. InterpretationActivity method_type LLM_JUDGEMENT. specified_by The prompt or workflow version. Required for AI lines. read_coverage, access_status How much of the document was read (TITLE_ONLY, ABSTRACT_ONLY, SECTIONS, FULL_TEXT) and whether it was open. Required on document-based lines. identifier_verified, grounding_checked Whether the cited id resolves and is about the topic, and whether the entities map to the claim's actual terms. sought_disputing_evidence Whether the search looked for evidence against the claim. reasoning_trace A link to the trace. The trace itself is not stored. SieveEvidenceLine confidence, confidence_basis The probability the evidence was read and linked correctly, and its basis (usually PRIOR for a pinned model version, MEASURED if a scorer evaluated this input). A confidence without a basis fails validation. data_quality_flags Flag known failures (QUOTE_NOT_FOUND, IDENTIFIER_UNRESOLVED, MISGROUNDED, SUSPECTED_HALLUCINATION). SieveAgent (registry) software_version, model_name, trust_levels The agent's version and model. Trust is maintained by the registry, from the agent's record of accepted and invalidated lines.

Confidence is data quality, not evidence strength. Put your read of how strongly the evidence bears on the claim in score_of_evidence_provided, and your read of whether you extracted and grounded it correctly in confidence.

docs.title: An example
docs.text:
Adapted from tests/data/profile/valid/c007_cf_cftr_panel.yaml (the passage text is illustrative):

id: sieve:pkt/MONDO_0009061-gene-HGNC_1884
type: EvidencePacket
version: "2026-10-10"
statement:
  id: sieve:st/MONDO_0009061-gene-HGNC_1884
  type: DiseaseAttributeStatement
  subject: MONDO:0009061              # cystic fibrosis
  predicate: {code: RO:0004003, label: has material basis in germline mutation in}
  object: HGNC:1884                   # CFTR
  review_state: NOT_VERIFIED
  proposing_channel: AI_AGENT
  has_evidence_lines:
    - id: sieve:el/cf-passage
      type: SieveEvidenceLine
      has_evidence_items: [sieve:tp/pmid-20301428-1]
      direction_of_evidence_provided: supports
      score_of_evidence_provided: 0.8
      confidence: 0.85
      confidence_basis: PRIOR
      contributions:
        - id: sieve:act/cf-passage
          type: InterpretationActivity
          contributor: sieve:agent/mondo-ai-extractor
          role: INTERPRETER
          date: "2026-10-10"
          method_type: LLM_JUDGEMENT
          specified_by: [sieve:method/evidence-extraction-prompt]
          read_coverage: FULL_TEXT
          access_status: OPEN_ACCESS
          identifier_verified: VERIFIED
          grounding_checked: VERIFIED
          sought_disputing_evidence: true
          run_id: mondo-ai-evidence-2026-10-10-r7
text_passages:
  - id: sieve:tp/pmid-20301428-1
    type: TextPassage
    statement_text: "Illustrative passage: cystic fibrosis is caused by pathogenic variants in CFTR."
    reported_in: [PMID:20301428]
    document_version: "2025-01"
    text_location: {section: Molecular Genetics, char_start: 1200, char_end: 1278}
    quote_verification: NOT_CHECKED    # VERIFIED only after a machine check
    contributions:
      - id: sieve:act/tp-extraction
        type: SieveContribution
        contributor: sieve:agent/mondo-ai-extractor
        role: EXTRACTOR
        date: "2026-10-10"
        specified_by: [sieve:method/evidence-extraction-prompt]
        run_id: mondo-ai-evidence-2026-10-10-r7
publications:
  - id: PMID:20301428
    type: Publication
    pmid: "20301428"
    resource: infores:pubmed
    generation_context:
      - {code: "PT:review", label: Review}

The full test file adds the resolution chain for "CFTR" (an LLM extraction step, then a lexical grounding step to HGNC:1884), an OMIM concordance line, a reviewer's LineStatusChange accepting the AI line unchanged, and a panel's decision.

docs.title: What happens to your lines
docs.text: A reviewer either accepts a line unchanged, or invalidates it, or writes a corrected line that supersedes it. Your line is never edited. Each outcome is recorded as a LineStatusChange and counts towards your agent's trust level.

docs.title: Validating your output
docs.text:
uv run linkml-validate -s schema/sieve.yaml -C EvidencePacket my_packet.yaml

import yaml
from sieve.profile_checks import check_packet

issues = check_packet(yaml.safe_load(open("my_packet.yaml")))
errors = [i for i in issues if i.severity == "ERROR"]

Quote dates in YAML for linkml-validate. check_packet catches what JSON Schema cannot, including a document-based line without read_coverage / access_status, an AI line without specified_by, a predicate outside the claim type's value set, evidence the claim type does not permit, and references to items that are not in the packet. Fix every ERROR before handing a packet off.

docs.title: DO / DON'T
docs.text:
DO

  • Quote source text verbatim, with its location and the document version.
  • Cite real, resolvable identifiers, and say whether you checked them.
  • Add a disputes line when the evidence cuts against the claim.
  • Record how much of the document you actually read.
  • State a confidence only with its basis.

DON'T

  • Don't fabricate references, PMIDs, quotes or concordances.
  • Don't set quote_verification: VERIFIED or identifier_verified: VERIFIED without a machine check.
  • Don't write assertion_decisions, review_state: VERIFIED or the statement score.
  • Don't fold data quality into strength: a shaky extraction gets a low confidence, not a low score_of_evidence_provided.
  • Don't use the pre-profile shape (status, has_evidence_lines, SieveDocument, ComputationalResult, items inlined in lines).

docs.title: Python API Reference
docs.text:
Application modules not yet migrated

sieve.datamodel, sieve.datamodel.codegen, sieve.profile_checks and sieve.traceability work with the current profile. sieve.datamodel.loaders, sieve.store, sieve.packet_ingest, sieve.packet_export and sieve.scoring still target the pre-profile model and fail at import or at run time. They are being migrated (issues/issue_migrate_app_to_profile.md). Their signatures are listed below as they are in the source.

For what the model fields mean, see the Data Model.

Module Purpose Status sieve.datamodel Generated Pydantic models current sieve.datamodel.codegen Generate the models from the schema current sieve.profile_checks Profile constraints beyond linkml-validate current sieve.traceability Requirement-to-schema traceability current sieve.datamodel.loaders Polymorphic packet loading pre-profile sieve.store PacketStore, DuckDB persistence pre-profile sieve.packet_ingest Validate and ingest YAML packets pre-profile sieve.packet_export RDF and YAML export pre-profile sieve.scoring Net Evidence Ratio pre-profile sieve.auth ORCID OAuth and curator authorisation model-independent

docs.title: sieve.datamodel
docs.text:
Pydantic v2 classes generated from schema/sieve.yaml into sieve.datamodel.sieve_models. The package re-exports the main ones:

from sieve.datamodel import (
    EvidencePacket, SieveRegistry,
    SieveStatement,                       # abstract; the ten claim types below
    TermExistenceStatement, DefinitionStatement, SynonymStatement,
    SubclassStatement, NegativeSubclassStatement, MappingStatement,
    DiseaseAttributeStatement, SubsetMembershipStatement,
    MetaclassStatement, ValueSetMembershipStatement,
    ExternalRecord, TextPassage, Publication, WebPage,
    ComputationalScore, InformationResource,
    SieveEvidenceLine, InterpretationActivity, AssertionDecision,
    SieveAgent, DecisionPolicy,
)

Everything else (GuidelineDocument, OriginEvent, ResolutionChain, AlignmentStep, AggregationRule, BatchSignOff, the enums, ...) is in sieve.datamodel.sieve_models. Field names are the schema's camelCase names. The type slot is a type designator, so validating a dict picks the concrete classes:

import yaml
from sieve.datamodel import EvidencePacket

data = yaml.safe_load(open("tests/data/profile/valid/c007_cf_cftr_panel.yaml"))
packet = EvidencePacket.model_validate(data)
type(packet.statement).__name__          # "DiseaseAttributeStatement"
packet.statement.score                   # 0.97
packet.text_passages[0].quote_verification # "NOT_CHECKED"

docs.title: sieve.datamodel.codegen
docs.text:
from sieve.datamodel.codegen import generate_pydantic, fix_date_shadowing

def generate_pydantic(schema_path: str | Path) -> str   # module source for the schema
def fix_date_shadowing(code: str) -> str                # alias the date type as _Date

The core's Activity.date slot shadows the date type inside generated class bodies on Python 3.10; fix_date_shadowing refers to the type through _Date instead. Run it through just gen-pydantic, or directly:

uv run python -m sieve.datamodel.codegen schema/sieve.yaml src/sieve/datamodel/sieve_models.py

docs.title: sieve.profile_checks
docs.text:
from sieve.profile_checks import check_packet, Issue, predicate_value_set, permitted_evidence

def check_packet(packet: dict[str, Any],
                 obsolete_terms: set[str] | frozenset[str] = frozenset()) -> list[Issue]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Issue:
    severity: Literal["ERROR", "WARNING"]
    code: str            # e.g. "PREDICATE_BINDING", "EVIDENCE_NOT_PERMITTED"
    message: str
    requirement: str     # the requirement ID the check enforces

def predicate_value_set(sv: SchemaView, claim_type: str) -> set[str]
def permitted_evidence(sv: SchemaView, claim_type: str) -> set[str]

check_packet takes a packet as a plain dict (as loaded from YAML or JSON) and returns an empty list when it passes. obsolete_terms lists Mondo terms known to be obsolete; subject obsolescence is read from term status, not stored on mappings.

Code Severity Requirement PREDICATE_BINDING ERROR predicate not in the claim type's value set (C00N) NEGATION ERROR NegativeSubclassStatement without negated: true, or a negated SubclassStatement (C005) PREFERRED_NOT_EXACT ERROR preferred on a mapping that is not skos:exactMatch (C006) DANGLING_REFERENCE ERROR a line references an item not in the packet (EINT.REQUIRED) EVIDENCE_NOT_PERMITTED ERROR item class not in the claim-evidence matrix (MATRIX.C00N) READ_COVERAGE ERROR document-based line without read_coverage / access_status (PROV.SA.EXECUTION) METHOD_REQUIRED ERROR AI or rule-based line without specified_by, or rule-based line without computed_by_rule (PROV.INTERP.METHODS) SUPERSEDED_NOT_INVALIDATED ERROR a superseded line is still VALID (EINT.FLAT_COLLAPSE) CHAIN_CONTIGUITY ERROR a resolution step does not read the previous step's output (PROV.SA.EXECUTION) BLIND_APPROVAL_EVIDENCE ERROR a review_depth: NONE decision contributes an evidence line OBSOLETE_TO_OBSOLETE, DEFINITION_WITHOUT_SOURCE, CONCORDANCE_DIRECTION, READ_COVERAGE_NOT_RECORDED WARNING states that need a person 
import yaml
from sieve.profile_checks import check_packet

packet = yaml.safe_load(open("tests/data/profile/valid/c005_down_syndrome_not_hereditary.yaml"))
check_packet(packet)                     # []
packet["statement"]["predicate"]["code"] = "skos:exactMatch"
check_packet(packet)
# [Issue(severity='ERROR', code='PREDICATE_BINDING',
#        message="skos:exactMatch is not a NegativeSubclassStatement predicate (['owl:equivalentClass', 'rdfs:subClassOf'])",
#        requirement='C005')]

docs.title: sieve.traceability
docs.text:
from sieve.traceability import (
    SCHEMA, CORE_SCHEMA, REQUIREMENTS_TSV, TRACEABILITY_YAML,   # paths
    load_requirements,     # () -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]  rows keyed by requirement ID
    load_traceability,     # () -> dict  {"modules": ..., "requirements": ...}
    schema_elements,       # (sv) -> list[(path, element)]  Class, Class.slot, Enum, Enum.value
    collect_annotations,   # (sv, key="requirements") -> dict[str, list[str]]
    render_markdown,       # (sv=None) -> str  the docs/requirements-traceability.md page
)

from linkml_runtime.utils.schemaview import SchemaView
from sieve.traceability import SCHEMA, collect_annotations, load_traceability

sv = SchemaView(str(SCHEMA))
collect_annotations(sv)["C005"]
# ['SieveStatement.negated', 'NegativeSubclassStatement', 'NegativeSubclassStatement.negated',
#  'ClaimType.NegativeSubclassStatement', 'SubclassPredicate']
load_traceability()["requirements"]["C005"]["disposition"]   # 'modelled'
collect_annotations(sv, key="decisions")["D-063"]            # elements behind decision D-063

just gen-traceability writes render_markdown() to docs/requirements-traceability.md.

docs.title: sieve.auth
docs.text:
ORCID OAuth login and curator authorisation for the Streamlit review UI. It does not use the data model.

from sieve.auth import (
    OrcidUser,                  # dataclass: orcid, name, access_token
    AuthorizedCurator,          # dataclass: orcid, name, role ("admin"|"curator")
    is_dev_mode,                # () -> bool  (SIEVE_DEV_MODE=true bypasses auth)
    is_orcid_configured,        # () -> bool
    get_orcid_config,           # () -> dict
    get_authorization_url,      # () -> str
    exchange_code_for_token,    # (code: str) -> OrcidUser | None
    load_authorized_curators,   # () -> dict[str, AuthorizedCurator]  (keyed by ORCID)
    is_authorized_curator,      # (orcid: str | None) -> bool  (True in dev mode)
    get_curator_role,           # (orcid: str | None) -> str | None
    is_admin,                   # (orcid: str | None) -> bool  (True in dev mode)
    get_curator_info,           # () -> tuple[str | None, str | None]  (orcid, name)
)

Authorised curators are read from curators.yaml (path overridable via the CURATORS_FILE env var), cached for 60 seconds:

curators:
  - orcid: "0000-0001-2345-6789"
    name: "Dr. Jane Smith"
    role: admin

Streamlit-bound helpers (get_current_user, set_current_user, logout, handle_oauth_callback, render_login_ui) require an active Streamlit session.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Application layer not yet migrated

The schema, the generated model, the profile checks and the traceability tooling below work with the current profile. The application layer (app.py, scoring.py, store.py, datamodel/loaders.py, packet_ingest.py, packet_export.py, cli.py and the LinkML-Map transforms) still targets the pre-profile model and is broken: it imports classes that no longer exist. It is being migrated (issues/issue_migrate_app_to_profile.md). Its description is kept here as a record of what it does.

For the packet shape, start with the Primer; for every field, see the Data Model.

docs.title: The pieces
docs.text: flowchart LR     CORE[schema/sepio_core.yamlSEPIO core, unchanged] --> PROF[schema/sieve.yamlSIEVE profile]     REQ[requirements/mondo_requirements.tsvtraceability.yaml] --> TRACE[sieve.traceability]     PROF --> TRACE     TRACE --> MD[docs/requirements-traceability.md]     PROF --> GEN[sieve.datamodel.codegen] --> PYD[datamodel/sieve_models.py]     PROF --> LV[linkml-validate]     PROF --> PC[sieve.profile_checks]     PKT[packet YAML / JSON] --> LV     PKT --> PC     PYD -.-> APP[application layerpre-profile, being migrated]

docs.title: schema/
docs.text:
• sepio_core.yaml: a byte-identical copy of the SEPIO core from sepio-linkml (commit 8c2c233). tests/test_profile_schema.py pins its hash, so it cannot be edited by accident.
  • sieve.yaml: the profile. It imports linkml:types and sepio_core, and every class specialises a core class. Narrowed core slots are declared in slot_usage. Predicate value sets are declared as bindings, and the claim-evidence matrix as a permitted_evidence annotation on each claim type.
  • minimal.yaml: the separate minimal microschema (see Minimal Evidence Model). It is not imported by the profile.

docs.title: datamodel/
docs.text:
• sieve_models.py: Pydantic v2 classes generated from schema/sieve.yaml. Regenerate with just gen-pydantic; tests/test_profile_schema.py fails if the checked-in file is stale.
  • codegen.py: wraps the LinkML Pydantic generator. The core's Activity.date slot shadows the date type in generated code on Python 3.10, so the generator output refers to the type through an alias instead of patching the core.
  • __init__.py: re-exports the packet, claim-type, item, line, provenance and registry classes.

The type slot is a type designator throughout, so EvidencePacket.model_validate(data) instantiates the concrete claim type and item classes without a custom loader.

docs.title: profile_checks.py
docs.text: check_packet(packet) runs the checks LinkML validation cannot express: predicate bindings, the claim-evidence matrix, dangling item references, read coverage and methods on AI and rule-based lines, resolution-chain contiguity, supersession, blind approvals, and WARNING states. It works on the packet as a plain dict, and every Issue names the requirement it enforces.

docs.title: traceability.py and requirements/
docs.text:
• requirements/mondo_requirements.tsv: the requirement rows, extracted from the Mondo requirements workbook by scripts/extract_requirements.py (just extract-requirements).
  • requirements/traceability.yaml: per requirement, its SEPIO design module, disposition (modelled, negative_constraint, not_desired, out_of_scope), decisions and rationale.
  • sieve.traceability joins those with the annotations.requirements on schema elements and renders docs/requirements-traceability.md (scripts/render_traceability.py, just gen-traceability).
  • tests/test_traceability.py keeps the three consistent, including that the rendered page is current.

docs.title: Application layer (pre-profile)
docs.text:
flowchart LR Y[YAML packetsinbox/] --> ING[packet_ingestvalidate + load] ING --> DB[(DuckDBPacketStore)] DB --> UI[app.pyStreamlit review] UI -->|rate items,record decisions| DB DB --> EXP[packet_exportRDF / YAML] CLI[cli.py] -.-> ING CLI -.-> EXP AUTH[auth.pyORCID] -.-> UI SCORE[scoring.pyNER] -.-> DB
  • datamodel/loaders.py: load_packet(path) / packet_from_dict(data) dispatched inlined evidence items to concrete classes by type: (EVIDENCE_ITEM_TYPES). The profile's type designators make this unnecessary; the module currently fails at import.
  • packet_ingest.py: validate_packet_dict(data), ingest_packet_file(path, store), ingest_packet_directory(path, store).
  • store.py: PacketStore, a DuckDB store (default data/sieve.duckdb) holding each packet as JSON plus promoted columns (evidence_packets) and a decision log (packet_decisions). Methods: insert_packet, get_packet, list_packets, get_stats, update_status, set_item_rating, record_decision, get_decisions.
  • scoring.py: net_evidence_ratio(packet), (S+ - S-) / (S+ + S- + S0) over line weights. To be replaced by the inclusion score S computed from the claim type's AggregationRule.
  • cli.py: Typer CLI with run, ingest, validate, export (see CLI Reference).
  • app.py: Streamlit app with Dashboard, Review Queue (per-item accept / reject, packet decisions), Ingest and Export views.
  • auth.py: ORCID OAuth with a curators.yaml allow-list; SIEVE_DEV_MODE=true bypasses login. It does not depend on the data model.
  • packet_export.py: packet_to_yaml, export_packets_to_yaml, packet_to_rdf, export_packets_to_rdf. RDF export wrote an owl:Axiom reifying the statement, linked to the packet by SEPIO:0000124, with oboInOwl:source annotations for accepted packets and IAO:0000233 for rejected and controversial ones.
  • transform/: LinkML-Map specs for DisMech → minimal → SIEVE. The second hop emits the pre-profile shape (see Minimal Evidence Model).

The migration maps the old flow onto the profile: packet status becomes review_state plus assertion_decisions, CurationDecision becomes AssertionDecision, per-item ratings become LineStatusChanges, and the Net Evidence Ratio becomes the inclusion score.

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text:
• Canonical core, unchanged. The profile narrows the core and never redefines it, so a SIEVE packet is SEPIO data and core updates can be taken by replacing one file.
  • Traceability next to the model. Requirement IDs sit on the schema elements that realise them, so the mapping cannot drift from the model; tests enforce both directions.
  • Two validation layers. JSON Schema (via linkml-validate) for structure and class rules; profile_checks for anything that reads inside a Coding or across references.
  • One packet per claim, versioned. Decisions name the packet version they were given on, so a change in evidence re-queues the claim instead of silently inheriting an old sign-off.
  • YAML packets: human-readable, diff-friendly, and easy to keep under version control next to ontology work.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
The sieve CLI targets the pre-profile model

sieve run, ingest, export and validate still target the pre-profile model. ingest, export and validate fail at import against the current schema. They are being migrated (issues/issue_migrate_app_to_profile.md). Until then, validate packets with linkml-validate and sieve.profile_checks, and maintain the generated artefacts with the just recipes below.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: uv sync --group dev

docs.title: Working commands
docs.text: Command What it does uv run linkml-validate -s schema/sieve.yaml -C EvidencePacket <file> Validate a packet against the profile (structure, enums, ranges, class rules) uv run linkml-validate -s schema/sieve.yaml -C SieveRegistry <file> Validate a registry of resources, agents, rules and policies just gen-pydantic Regenerate src/sieve/datamodel/sieve_models.py from the schema just gen-traceability Regenerate docs/requirements-traceability.md just extract-requirements [workbook] Re-extract requirements/mondo_requirements.tsv from the Mondo requirements workbook just gen-docs Regenerate the schema reference in docs/elements/ just serve-docs Regenerate the schema reference and serve the docs locally

docs.title: linkml-validate
docs.text:
uv run linkml-validate -s schema/sieve.yaml -C EvidencePacket packet.yaml

Prints No issues found or one [ERROR] line per problem, and exits 1 on errors. It checks required fields, ranges, enums (Direction, ReviewState, AssertionRoute, ...), numeric bounds (line score_of_evidence_provided in [0, 1], inclusion score in [-1, 1]) and the class rules (policy and provider routes only accept and name their policy; batch decisions name batch and review depth; a confidence needs a basis). The validator is closed, so unknown fields are errors.

Quote dates in YAML (date: "2026-10-20"). Unquoted dates are parsed into date objects and rejected as "not of type 'string'". Predicate bindings and the claim-evidence matrix are not checked here; run sieve.profile_checks.check_packet for those (see Workflows).

docs.title: just extract-requirements
docs.text:
just extract-requirements                                   # ../../notes/evidence/background/mondo-requirements/...
just extract-requirements /path/to/Mondo_Requirements_Collection_Forms.xlsx

Writes one row per requirement (category rows skipped) to requirements/mondo_requirements.tsv. tests/test_traceability.py compares the TSV with the workbook when the workbook is checked out.

Starts the Streamlit app (dashboard, review queue, ingest and export views).

sieve validate (-i <file> | -I <dir>)

Validates each file as an EvidencePacket against schema/sieve.yaml, prints one line per error and a summary, and exits 1 on any error. It currently fails at import; use linkml-validate as above.

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
This is the reference for the SIEVE evidence model. For the concepts in plain terms, read the Primer first.

SIEVE is a profile of the SEPIO core information model, in two LinkML files:

  • schema/sepio_core.yaml: the canonical SEPIO core, copied unchanged from sepio-linkml (commit 8c2c233) and pinned by hash in tests/test_profile_schema.py.
  • schema/sieve.yaml: the profile (id: https://w3id.org/sieve). It imports the core, and every class in it specialises a core class. Inherited slots keep or narrow their core range. Nothing in the core is redefined.

Names follow the core's camelCase. The profile was built from the Mondo requirements collection: each class, slot and enum value that realises a requirement carries the requirement ID in annotations.requirements, and the decision-log IDs behind it in annotations.decisions. The requirement-by-requirement mapping is on the Requirements Traceability page, generated from those annotations.

Generated reference

Every class, slot and enum has a generated page under the Schema Reference. This page is the guided tour.

docs.title: The shape of the data
docs.text:
• One EvidencePacket per claim. A packet (is_a DataSet) holds one claim-type statement, the evidence items its lines refer to, and a required version. A change to its lines, items or score makes a new version (previous_version points back). Packets are never deleted: a rejected claim stays on record with its evidence and decisions.
  • Lines live on the statement, items live on the packet. Evidence lines are inlined under statement.has_evidence_lines. Evidence items sit in typed lists on the packet (external_records, prior_claims, text_passages, publications, web_pages, guidelines, computational_scores), and lines refer to them by id.
  • Shared reference data is maintained in a SieveRegistry. Information resources, source releases, agents, methods, aggregation rules, decision policies and batch sign-offs are maintained once there.
  • A packet is self-contained. Its required reference_snapshot (a SieveRegistry) holds a frozen copy, as of the packet version, of every registry entry the packet references. Every reference must resolve inside the packet (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE in sieve.profile_checks), so revising the registry never changes how an existing packet version reads (D-049, D-051, D-060).
  • Released artefacts are EvidencePacketCollections. Encoding provenance (which pipeline serialised the dump, with which export rules) is recorded there, never per claim.
  • Every entity carries id and type. type is the type designator, so a loader or validator knows which claim type, item class or activity it is looking at.
flowchart TD P["EvidencePacketid, version"] --> S["Statement (one claim type)subject, predicate, object, negated"] S --> L["SieveEvidenceLinedirection, strength, score"] L --> IA["InterpretationActivitywho, when, how"] S --> D["AssertionDecisionoutcome, route, S, packet version"] S --> O["OriginEventcopied / cloned / inspired by"] P --> I["typed item listsexternal_records, prior_claims,text_passages, publications, ..."] L -. "has_evidence_items (ids)" .-> I R[("SieveRegistryresources, releases, agents,methods, rules, policies, batches")] L -. "computed_by_rule" .-> R D -. "policy, batch, aggregation_rule" .-> R

docs.title: SEPIO design modules
docs.text:
The core names no modules, so the profile groups its classes into six, following the core's class groups. Each requirement is assigned to one module in requirements/traceability.yaml.

Module SEPIO core classes Profile classes statement Statement, Proposition, Qualifier SieveStatement and the ten claim types evidence-item InformationEntity, Document, DataItem, DataSet, StudyResult ExternalRecord, TextPassage, Publication, WebPage, GuidelineDocument, ComputationalScore, InformationResource, SourceRelease, EvidencePacket evidence-line EvidenceLine SieveEvidenceLine, LineStatusChange provenance Activity, Contribution, Agent, Method SieveAgent, SieveMethod, AggregationRule, DecisionPolicy, BatchSignOff, SieveContribution, InterpretationActivity, AssertionDecision, OriginEvent, ResolutionChain, AlignmentStep record-metadata RecordMetadata RetrievalMetadata utility Coding, Extension, Qualifier TextLocation, QualityRating, LevelAssignment, AppliedRule

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
SieveStatement (abstract, is_a Statement) is a Mondo claim as an identified, reified statement. Subject, predicate and object sit directly on the statement. There are no Proposition objects: the core proposition slot is inherited but unused, and concordance and dispute are matched on subject, predicate, object and negated.

Field Range Req Description subject uriorcurie Yes The Mondo term the claim is about. predicate Coding Yes The relation. Each claim type binds it to a value set. object string / uriorcurie Yes Term, text or value, depending on the claim type. negated boolean No The claim is that subject-predicate-object does not hold. Default false. statement_text string No Human-readable rendering of the claim. review_state ReviewState Yes NOT_VERIFIED (default), PENDING_REVIEW, VERIFIED. Workflow state, distinct from the decision outcome. proposing_channel ProposingChannel No Who proposed the claim (curator, source ingest, lexical pipeline, AI agent, ...). Selects the claim prior. has_evidence_lines SieveEvidenceLine[] No The evidence lines, inlined. has_evidence ids No Direct claim-to-item links with no interpretation. has_evidence_from_sources InformationResource ids No Source-level attribution without a record id (e.g. MONDO:DOID). origin OriginEvent[] No Where the claim was copied, cloned or adapted from. assertion_decisions AssertionDecision[] No Decision history, oldest first. contributions SieveContribution[] No Non-asserting roles: provider, stakeholder, endorser. score float, [-1, 1] No The current inclusion score S. strength string No The band of S, as declared by the rule that computed it. direction Direction No The sign of S.

Each concrete subclass is one claim type. It binds predicate to its value set (bindings) and lists the evidence-item classes it accepts in a permitted_evidence annotation (the claim-evidence matrix).

ID Class Predicates Permitted evidence C001 TermExistenceStatement rdf:type, owl:deprecated, IAO:0100001, oboInOwl:consider ExternalRecord, prior claim, Publication, GuidelineDocument C002 DefinitionStatement IAO:0000115 Publication, WebPage C003 SynonymStatement oboInOwl:has{Exact,Related,Narrow,Broad}Synonym ExternalRecord, prior claim, TextPassage, Publication, WebPage, ComputationalScore C004 SubclassStatement rdfs:subClassOf, owl:equivalentClass ExternalRecord, prior claim, TextPassage, Publication, WebPage, GuidelineDocument C005 NegativeSubclassStatement as C004, with negated: true ExternalRecord, prior claim, Publication C006 MappingStatement skos:exactMatch, broadMatch, narrowMatch, relatedMatch ExternalRecord, prior claim, ComputationalScore C007 DiseaseAttributeStatement RO:0004003, RO:0000053, RO:0004029, RO:0004026, RO:0014001, RO:0002162, mondoRel:predisposes_towards ExternalRecord, prior claim, TextPassage, Publication, WebPage, GuidelineDocument C008 SubsetMembershipStatement oboInOwl:inSubset ExternalRecord, prior claim C009 MetaclassStatement (candidate) sieve:isKindOfClass; object is a DiseaseKind ExternalRecord, prior claim C010 ValueSetMembershipStatement (candidate) sieve:memberOfRecordScope ExternalRecord, prior claim

Some claim types add qualifiers: obsolescence_reason and scheduled_obsoletion_date on C001; preferred, valid_direction and object_obsolete_in_source_version on C006. C004 represents a logical definition as one statement per intersection_of element. C009 and C010 use sieve: placeholder IRIs for their predicates.

docs.title: Evidence items
docs.text:
An evidence item is the information interpreted as evidence. Whether an item is evidence (corroboration) or origin depends on where it is referenced: from an evidence line, or from statement.origin.

Class Core parent Packet list What it is ExternalRecord InformationEntity external_records A record in an external database or terminology (DOID:14250, OMIM:219700), as read from a release. Requires resource and record_metadata; obsolete_in_source flags obsolete records. any claim type (e.g. SubclassStatement) Statement prior_claims A prior claim a source makes, in its own identifiers (DOID:14250 is_a DOID:630), typed by what it claims, never by its role. reported_in names the record; groundings records how each id was resolved to Mondo; own_log_odds is set when a competing-claim line cites it (D-069). TextPassage Statement text_passages A verbatim passage (statement_text) from a document (reported_in). Created in the Mondo ecosystem, so it requires its extraction contributions and a quote_verification outcome. Publication Document publications A PMID, DOI or ISBN. Publications sharing a reports_study key are not independent. WebPage Document web_pages A non-scholarly page (GARD, MedlinePlus, Wikipedia). GitHub issues are not web-page evidence: they go in a contribution's context. GuidelineDocument Document guidelines A guideline or consensus document. ComputationalScore DataItem computational_scores A computed score (lexical match, Boomer, AI score): value, the method in specified_by, software_version, parameters.

Two mixins supply the shared slots. EvidenceItem marks everything a line can point at (including lines themselves, for higher-order lines). UpstreamItem marks items made outside Mondo and adds resource, generation_context (study type or curation basis; sieve:basis_unknown when the source does not say) and resource_role_override.

The registry describes sources as a whole. An InformationResource has a default_role (PRIMARY or AGGREGATOR), derives_content_from (dependence between sources) and dated quality_ratings. A SourceRelease is one versioned snapshot of a resource.

docs.title: Evidence lines
docs.text:
SieveEvidenceLine (is_a EvidenceLine) is one evidentiary judgement: these items bear on the enclosing claim, in this direction, with this strength. Its target is always the enclosing statement, so the core target_proposition is unused.

Field Range Req Description has_evidence_items ids No Items (or other lines) this line interprets. direction_of_evidence_provided Direction Yes supports or disputes. There is no neutral. strength_of_evidence_provided string No Categorical band, from the rule's strength_bands. score_of_evidence_provided float, [0, 1] No Strength on the shared 0-1 scale. Direction is not carried by the sign. contributions InterpretationActivity[] Yes The interpretation act. A collective act is one contribution with participants. computed_by_rule AggregationRule id No Required for rule-based lines (profile check). confidence, confidence_basis float [0, 1], ConfidenceBasis No Data quality. A confidence requires a basis (class rule). data_quality_flags DataQualityFlag[] No Failure flags that gate the line (QUOTE_NOT_FOUND, SUSPECTED_HALLUCINATION, ...). independence_cluster string No Cluster assigned by the rule. Only the strongest line per cluster counts. validity, status_changes, supersedes LineValidity, LineStatusChange[], ids No Invalidation and supersession history. date_attached, last_confirmed, last_confirmed_against date, date, SourceRelease id No When the evidence was attached and last confirmed against a release.

Lines are immutable. A misreading is corrected by a new line that supersedes the old one. The old line becomes INVALIDATED, stays on record and is excluded from the score. A LineStatusChange records who invalidated, superseded or accepted a line, when and why. That is also where a reviewer's verdict on an AI's line goes.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text: Class is_a Role SieveAgent Agent A person (ORCID), organisation or group, or software. Dated roles and trust_levels; software_version and model_name for software; members for panels. SieveMethod Method A versioned method: guideline, workflow, prompt version, export rule set. AggregationRule SieveMethod Per claim type: line strengths, strength_bands, confidence_floor. Computes S. DecisionPolicy SieveMethod A human-approved procedure under which an automated system may accept claims: scope, acceptance_threshold, pinned rules. It can only accept. BatchSignOff Activity A one-off curator approval of a filtered result set: re-runnable filter_query, frozen result_set of packet@version, review_bands. SieveContribution Contribution An agent's act, with role, participants, and agent_role_at_time / agent_trust_at_time snapshotted as of the act; context (issue, PR, call), run_id, perspective. InterpretationActivity SieveContribution The act behind a line: date, method_type, read_coverage, access_status, and the checks an AI act records (identifier_verified, grounding_checked, sought_disputing_evidence, reasoning_trace). AssertionDecision SieveContribution The decision on the claim (see below). OriginEvent Activity How the claim entered Mondo: derivation_type (CLONED_FROM, COPIED_FROM, INSPIRED_BY), source_item, source_label, source_release, pipeline and date. ResolutionChain Activity How a source id or mention was resolved to the target id: ordered steps for one entity_slot, with chain_confidence. AlignmentStep Activity One extraction, translation, grounding or normalisation step: input_value, output_value, method, quality_category, confidence + basis, mapping set and version, review_status.

docs.title: Record metadata
docs.text: RetrievalMetadata (is_a RecordMetadata) says where and when a concrete record was read: retrieved_from (resource), source_release or source_version, retrieval_date and the source's own label at the time (source_label). It is required on ExternalRecord. EvidencePacketCollection.record_metadata carries artefact-level encoding provenance.

docs.title: Utilities
docs.text: The core Coding (code, label, system, system_version) types the predicate and generation context. The profile adds TextLocation (section, character offsets), QualityRating (dated level, optionally per claim type), LevelAssignment (dated role or trust level, optionally per domain) and AppliedRule (a named alignment rule with its certainty).

docs.title: Two levels of judgement
docs.text:
SIEVE keeps two judgements apart:

  1. Evidence line: does this item bear on the claim, which way, how strongly? Made by an interpreter (curator, panel, pipeline, AI agent), recorded with its InterpretationActivity, immutable once made.
  2. AssertionDecision: does the claim go into Mondo? Made over all lines, and recorded with what it was given on.
Field Description outcome ACCEPTED, REJECTED, CONTROVERSIAL, DEFERRED. route INDIVIDUAL_SIGN_OFF, CONSENSUS_SIGN_OFF, DELEGATED_POLICY, PROVIDER_AUTHORITY, BATCH_SIGN_OFF. inclusion_score, score_band, aggregation_rule S at decision time, its band, and the rule version that computed it. signed_packet_version The packet version decided on. A later version re-queues the claim. policy, threshold_passed For policy routes. batch, review_depth For batch sign-offs. A NONE-depth approval adds no evidence. evidence_line The expert line this decision contributed, if any. contributor, date, rationale, context Who decided, when, why, where.

Every claim rests on a human decision, made per claim (sign-off, consensus, batch) or per policy. Class rules enforce that automated routes (DELEGATED_POLICY, PROVIDER_AUTHORITY) can only accept and must name their policy, and that a batch decision names its batch and review depth. Decisions accumulate: claims are re-evaluated when rules, policies or evidence change.

docs.title: Three axes: provenance, evidence, data quality
docs.text:
Three questions are recorded separately, so one cannot stand in for another:

  • Provenance: where did this come from, and who did what? OriginEvent, ResolutionChain, contributions and retrieval metadata. "Cloned from OMIM" is origin, not evidence that the term is right.
  • Evidence: does it support or dispute the claim, and how strongly? Line direction_of_evidence_provided and score_of_evidence_provided in [0, 1].
  • Data quality: was the evidence read and linked correctly? SEPIO confidence on lines and alignment steps, with a required confidence_basis (MEASURED, DETERMINISTIC, PRIOR). Confidence gates or discounts a line. It never rewrites the line's strength.

docs.title: The inclusion score
docs.text:
statement.score is the inclusion score S in [-1, 1]: one number saying whether the claim should be in Mondo. The claim type's AggregationRule computes it (decision D-063):

w_i = d_i * s_i * q_i * c_i     direction (+1/-1), strength, source prior, confidence
one line per independence cluster (the strongest)
L   = L0 + k * sum(w_i)          L0 = claim prior (claim type + proposing channel)
S   = tanh(L / 2)                = 2 * P(true) - 1

Lines whose confidence is below the rule's confidence_floor are excluded. Above it, confidence discounts the line, so a misread contributes nothing rather than negative evidence. statement.strength is the band of S and statement.direction its sign. S is computed, not asserted: a signer's view goes in as an expert line, not as an edit to S. The S that a decision was given on is copied to AssertionDecision.inclusion_score.

The scoring code has not been written for this model yet. The values in the example packets are illustrative (see issues/issue_migrate_app_to_profile.md).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Two layers check a packet.

linkml-validate checks ranges, enums, cardinality and the class rules:

uv run linkml-validate -s schema/sieve.yaml -C EvidencePacket packet.yaml
uv run linkml-validate -s schema/sieve.yaml -C SieveRegistry registry.yaml

Quote dates in YAML

linkml-validate parses unquoted YAML dates (date: 2026-10-20) into date objects, which the generated JSON Schema rejects. Quote them (date: "2026-10-20") or validate a JSON copy. The test suite loads YAML with dates kept as strings.

sieve.profile_checks.check_packet covers what linkml-validate cannot: predicate bindings, the claim-evidence matrix, dangling references, read coverage on document-based lines, methods on AI and rule-based lines, chain contiguity, supersession and blind approvals. It also reports WARNING states that need a person (obsolete-to-obsolete mappings, definitions with no source, read coverage not recorded). Every issue names the requirement it enforces. See the Python API.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
A mapping claim accepted in a batch sign-off, adapted from tests/data/profile/valid/c006_down_syndrome_icd10cm_batch.yaml. The ids sieve:rule/..., sieve:batch/..., sieve:release/... and infores:... resolve in the packet's own reference_snapshot, a frozen copy of the entries in the registry (tests/data/profile/registry.yaml). The snapshot is left out of the excerpt below.

id: sieve:pkt/MONDO_0008608-exact-ICD10CM_Q90
type: EvidencePacket
version: "2026-10-25"
statement:
  id: sieve:st/MONDO_0008608-exact-ICD10CM_Q90
  type: MappingStatement
  subject: MONDO:0008608
  predicate: {code: skos:exactMatch}
  object: ICD10CM:Q90
  preferred: true
  valid_direction: BOTH
  review_state: VERIFIED
  proposing_channel: LEXICAL_PIPELINE
  score: 0.93
  strength: strong
  direction: supports
  has_evidence_lines:
    - id: sieve:el/q90-lexical
      type: SieveEvidenceLine
      has_evidence_items: [sieve:score/q90-lexical]
      direction_of_evidence_provided: supports
      strength_of_evidence_provided: weak
      score_of_evidence_provided: 0.3
      computed_by_rule: sieve:rule/mapping-v1.0
      contributions:
        - id: sieve:act/q90-lexical
          type: InterpretationActivity
          contributor: sieve:agent/concordance-pipeline
          date: "2026-10-24"
          method_type: RULE_BASED_STRENGTH
          specified_by: [sieve:method/mondo-mapping-guide]
    - id: sieve:el/q90-record
      type: SieveEvidenceLine
      has_evidence_items: [ICD10CM:Q90]
      direction_of_evidence_provided: supports
      strength_of_evidence_provided: strong
      score_of_evidence_provided: 0.8
      computed_by_rule: sieve:rule/mapping-v1.0
      contributions:
        - id: sieve:act/q90-record
          type: InterpretationActivity
          contributor: orcid:0000-0001-5208-3432
          date: "2026-10-25"
          method_type: EXPERT_JUDGEMENT
          specified_by: [sieve:method/mondo-mapping-guide]
          read_coverage: STRUCTURED_RECORD
  assertion_decisions:
    - id: sieve:dec/q90-batch
      type: AssertionDecision
      contributor: orcid:0000-0001-5208-3432
      date: "2026-10-25"
      outcome: ACCEPTED
      route: BATCH_SIGN_OFF
      batch: sieve:batch/mappings-2026-10-25
      review_depth: EYEBALLED
      inclusion_score: 0.93
      score_band: strong
      aggregation_rule: sieve:rule/mapping-v1.0
      signed_packet_version: "2026-10-25"
external_records:
  - id: ICD10CM:Q90
    type: ExternalRecord
    label: Down syndrome
    resource: infores:icd10cm
    record_metadata:
      retrieved_from: infores:icd10cm
      source_release: sieve:release/icd10cm-2026
      retrieval_date: "2026-10-01"
      source_label: Down syndrome
computational_scores:
  - id: sieve:score/q90-lexical
    type: ComputationalScore
    value: "0.97"
    specified_by: [sieve:method/lexmatch]
    software_version: oak-0.6
    parameters: "normalize=true"

The other examples in tests/data/profile/valid/ cover a synonym accepted under a policy (C003), a negative subclass claim with disputing evidence (C005) and a gene-disease claim with an AI-extracted passage and a panel sign-off (C007). More packets are in inbox/examples/.

docs.title: Coming from the pre-profile model
docs.text:
The earlier snake_case model (sepio_classes.yaml, status, ConcordanceItem, ...) is gone. Roughly:

Before Now status, CurationDecision statement.review_state + statement.assertion_decisions items inlined in lines items in typed packet lists, referenced by id ConcordanceItem a prior claim, e.g. SynonymStatement (the claim) + ExternalRecord (the record) SieveDocument with quote Publication / WebPage / GuidelineDocument, plus TextPassage for the quote ComputationalResult ComputationalScore AgentContribution an expert line with its InterpretationActivity, or a SieveContribution item rating LineStatusChange on the line neutral direction removed: lines support or dispute Net Evidence Ratio inclusion score S

docs.title: The Minimal Evidence Microschema
docs.text:
This page introduces the minimal evidence microschema — a small, standalone model for "evidence that supports or disputes a claim" that any Monarch project can import and reuse — and shows it working on a real record: a DisMech pathophysiology assertion for Fanconi Anemia is transformed into the minimal model.

just transform-dismech   # DisMech -> minimal, output validated against schema/minimal.yaml

Status

The minimal model is provisional pending coordination with the SEPIO project (schema id and the enum-to-ontology meaning: IRIs are not yet final). See the design spec specs/2026-07-31-minimal-microschema-and-sieve-alignment-design.md. That spec's alignment with the full SIEVE model no longer holds: SIEVE has since been rebuilt as a camelCase profile of the SEPIO core, and the two schemas are not connected (see Relation to the SIEVE profile).

docs.title: Why a minimal model
docs.text:
Many projects independently model the same thing — a claim, and the evidence for or against it — and each does it slightly differently. The minimal microschema is the small shared core everyone can agree on: one EvidenceLine grouping one or more TextSpan evidence items, each drawn from a Document. It is deliberately lean so it is easy to adopt, and it is SEPIO-aligned by class_uri/slot_uri (not by importing SEPIO), so its instances are SEPIO evidence without dragging in the whole SEPIO model.

flowchart LR subgraph minimal["minimal microschema"] C[EvidencedClaim] -->|has_evidence_lines| L[EvidenceLine] L -->|has_evidence_items| T[TextSpan · the 'A' shape] T -->|reported_in| D[Document] L -.direction_of_evidence_provided.-> Dir([Direction]) L -.evidence_source.-> Src([EvidenceSource · ECO]) end

The model has three concepts and three enums:

Concept What it is SEPIO class_uri EvidencedClaim a claim plus the evidence lines bearing on it sepio:Statement EvidenceLine one line of reasoning, with a single direction + source sepio:EvidenceLine TextSpan (A) a verbatim text span used as evidence, plus its document sepio:DataItem Document the publication a span was drawn from sepio:Document

Direction (SUPPORTS/REFUTES/NEUTRAL — polarity only), Strength (STRONG/MODERATE/WEAK — kept separate from direction), EvidenceSource (HUMAN_CLINICAL/MODEL_ORGANISM/…, each mapping onto an ECO branch), and DocumentType round it out. A future TextMiningResult (C) will subclass TextSpan to carry extraction metadata (score, offsets, method) — so the minimal "A" shape stays valid while richer "C" evidence is is-a compatible.

docs.title: The transform, in one picture
docs.text:
flowchart LR DM[DisMech recordFanconi Anemia] -->|"dismech_to_minimal(linkml-map)"| MIN[minimalEvidencedClaim] MIN -->|"minimal_to_sieve(linkml-map, pre-profile)"| SV[sieveEvidencePacket] MIN -. validates .-> MS[(schema/minimal.yaml)] SV -. "fails: pre-profile shape" .-> SS[(schema/sieve.yaml)]

Both hops are linkml-map transformation specs in transform/. Only the first works today; the second still targets the pre-profile SIEVE model. The source shape is a vendored snapshot of DisMech's model (transform/dismech_source.yaml) so the pipeline runs without the DisMech repo checked out.

docs.title: Before: a DisMech assertion
docs.text:
DisMech records pathophysiology as a claim (name + description) with a flat list of evidence items. Each item is a verbatim snippet from a reference, tagged with a supports direction and an evidence_source. Here is the "Hematopoietic Stem Cell Attrition" node from the Fanconi Anemia record (transform/dismech_fanconi_input.yaml), lightly trimmed:

name: Hematopoietic Stem Cell Attrition
description: Progressive depletion of long-term hematopoietic stem cells ...
evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38424108
    reference_title: "Deregulated protein homeostasis constrains fetal HSC pool expansion in Fanconi anemia."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: "proteostasis deregulation itself is driven by excess sterile inflammatory activity ..."
    explanation: Demonstrates that inflammatory signaling drives HSC pool deficits in FA ...
  - reference: PMID:24037726
    reference_title: "Variant ALDH2 is associated with accelerated progression of bone marrow failure ..."
    supports: PARTIAL
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "the FA proteins might counteract aldehyde-induced genotoxicity in hematopoietic stem cells"
    explanation: Establishes that aldehydes cause genotoxicity in HSCs ...

docs.title: After: the minimal model
docs.text:
The transform (transform/dismech_to_minimal.transform.yaml) makes the assertion an EvidencedClaim and turns each DisMech evidence item into its own EvidenceLine holding a single TextSpan. The per-item supports/evidence_source — which DisMech stores on the item — move up to the line, matching the minimal rule that one line has one direction and one source. Crucially, DisMech's supports enum conflates three things, so the transform splits it: SUPPORT/REFUTE become the direction; PARTIAL becomes direction: SUPPORTS plus strength: WEAK (partial support is a strength, not a direction); and the operational values (NO_EVIDENCE, WRONG_STATEMENT) are curation signals that don't belong in the evidence model at all. The snippet becomes the span's value, and reference + reference_title become its Document:

statement_text: Hematopoietic Stem Cell Attrition
has_evidence_lines:
  - direction_of_evidence_provided: SUPPORTS
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    description: Demonstrates that inflammatory signaling drives HSC pool deficits in FA ...
    has_evidence_items:
      - value: "proteostasis deregulation itself is driven by excess sterile inflammatory activity ..."
        reported_in:
          id: PMID:38424108
          title: "Deregulated protein homeostasis constrains fetal HSC pool expansion in Fanconi anemia."
  - direction_of_evidence_provided: SUPPORTS
    strength_of_evidence_provided: WEAK      # dismech PARTIAL -> direction + strength
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    description: Establishes that aldehydes cause genotoxicity in HSCs ...
    has_evidence_items:
      - value: "the FA proteins might counteract aldehyde-induced genotoxicity in hematopoietic stem cells"
        reported_in:
          id: PMID:24037726
          title: "Variant ALDH2 is associated with accelerated progression of bone marrow failure ..."

This output validates against schema/minimal.yaml.

One line per item — and when to merge

The mechanical transform gives one line per DisMech item. That is correct here, because the two items differ in source (model organism vs human clinical) and strength (full vs partial/WEAK). When several items share a direction and strength and source and document, a curation step may merge them into a single line with several has_evidence_items — an EvidenceLine is a line of reasoning, not a sentence.

docs.title: Relation to the SIEVE profile
docs.text:
The minimal model is currently not connected to SIEVE. The SIEVE profile (schema/sieve.yaml) imports the canonical SEPIO core unchanged and uses its camelCase names. schema/minimal.yaml is unchanged: snake_case, standalone, and aligned with SEPIO only through class_uri / slot_uri. A minimal instance is therefore not a valid SIEVE packet, and nothing in sieve.yaml refers to minimal.yaml.

The second transform (transform/minimal_to_sieve.transform.yaml) still emits the pre-profile SIEVE shape (SieveDocument items, snake_case slots, status), which the profile rejects, so just transform-minimal-to-sieve and just transform-all fail at their last validation step. How the two schemas should relate again (a sub-profile of the core, a transform as the formal bridge, a camelCase standalone kernel, or no separate kernel) is open: issues/issue_minimal_kernel_vs_profile.md.

For orientation, the nearest counterparts in the profile (not a decided mapping):

Minimal SIEVE profile EvidencedClaim a claim-type statement (SubclassStatement, DiseaseAttributeStatement, ...) with SPO on the statement, inside a versioned EvidencePacket EvidenceLine SieveEvidenceLine, which also requires the InterpretationActivity that produced it TextSpan, inlined in the line TextPassage in the packet's text_passages, referenced from the line by id, with its extraction provenance Document, inlined via reported_in Publication in the packet's publications, referenced from TextPassage.reported_in Direction (SUPPORTS / REFUTES / NEUTRAL) Direction (supports / disputes; no neutral) Strength strength_of_evidence_provided (band) and score_of_evidence_provided (0-1) evidence_source (ECO branch) no direct slot; the nearest is the item's generation_context

See the Data Model for the profile.
