docs.text: File Role schema/minimal.yaml the minimal microschema transform/dismech_source.yaml vendored snapshot of the DisMech evidence shape transform/dismech_fanconi_input.yaml the input Fanconi assertion transform/dismech_to_minimal.transform.yaml DisMech → minimal transform transform/minimal_to_sieve.transform.yaml minimal → sieve transform (pre-profile target, currently fails) project.justfile transform-dismech, transform-minimal-to-sieve, transform-all tests/test_transform_dismech.py runs the pipeline and validates both outputs (the SIEVE stage currently fails)

docs.title: ORCID OAuth Setup Guide
docs.text: This guide will help you set up ORCID authentication for Sieve. ORCID provides OAuth 2.0 authentication that works seamlessly on localhost for development.

docs.title: Step 1: Create a Sandbox ORCID Account (for testing)
docs.text:
1. Go to https://sandbox.orcid.org/register
  2. Create a test account (this is separate from your real ORCID)
  3. Verify your email

Note: The sandbox is completely separate from production ORCID. Any test accounts or credentials created here won't affect your real ORCID record.

docs.title: Step 2: Register Your Application
docs.text:
1. Log in to https://sandbox.orcid.org
  2. Click your name in the top right → Developer Tools
  3. If prompted, accept the developer agreement
  4. Click Register for the free ORCID public API

Fill in the form: - Name of your application: Sieve Curation App (or any name you like) - Website URL: http://localhost:8501 - Description: Ontology assertion curation tool - Redirect URIs: http://localhost:8501/

Important: The redirect URI must include the trailing slash and match exactly!

  1. Click Save

docs.title: Step 3: Get Your Credentials
docs.text:
After saving, you'll see your credentials: - Client ID: Looks like APP-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX - Client Secret: Click "Show" to reveal it (looks like a UUID)

Copy both of these values.

docs.title: Step 4: Configure Sieve
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the project root (copy from .env.example):

cp .env.example .env

Edit .env with your credentials:

ORCID_SANDBOX=true
ORCID_CLIENT_ID=APP-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
ORCID_CLIENT_SECRET=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
ORCID_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:8501/

docs.title: Step 5: (Optional) Load the .env automatically
docs.text:
The app already loads .env on startup (app.py calls load_dotenv(override=True)), so a .env file in the project root is picked up with no extra setup.

Alternatively, you can export the variables in your shell instead of using a .env file:

export ORCID_SANDBOX=true
export ORCID_CLIENT_ID=APP-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
export ORCID_CLIENT_SECRET=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
export ORCID_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:8501/

docs.title: Step 6: Run the App
docs.text:
uv run streamlit run src/sieve/app.py

You should see a "Login with ORCID" button in the sidebar. Click it to authenticate with your sandbox ORCID account.

docs.title: Switching to Production
docs.text:
When ready to use real ORCID accounts:

  1. Register your app at https://orcid.org/developer-tools (same process as sandbox)
  2. Update your .env: 
    ORCID_SANDBOX=false
ORCID_CLIENT_ID=APP-YYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY
ORCID_CLIENT_SECRET=yyyyyyyy-yyyy-yyyy-yyyy-yyyyyyyyyyyy

docs.title: "Login with ORCID" button not appearing
docs.text: If you see the manual ORCID entry fields instead of the login button, the OAuth credentials are not configured. Check: - The .env file exists and has correct values - The environment variables are loaded (try python-dotenv or export manually)

docs.title: "Failed to authenticate with ORCID"
docs.text:
• Verify your Client ID and Secret are correct
  • Check that the Redirect URI in your .env matches exactly what you registered with ORCID (including trailing slash)
  • Make sure you're using sandbox credentials with ORCID_SANDBOX=true

docs.title: Redirect URI mismatch
docs.text: ORCID is strict about redirect URIs. Ensure: - You registered http://localhost:8501/ (with trailing slash) - Your ORCID_REDIRECT_URI env var is http://localhost:8501/ - You're accessing the app at http://localhost:8501 (not 127.0.0.1)

docs.title: Security Notes
docs.text:
• Never commit your .env file or expose your Client Secret
  • The .env file is already in .gitignore
  • For production, use proper secret management (environment variables, secret managers)

docs.title: SIEVE in Plain Terms
docs.text:
SIEVE records why Mondo believes a claim, and packages that "why" so a curator, or a machine, can check it.

A claim is one statement about a Mondo term, for example:

Down syndrome is not a subclass of hereditary disease

SIEVE puts that claim, the evidence for and against it, and the decisions taken on it into one evidence packet:

id: sieve:pkt/MONDO_0008608-excl-MONDO_0003847
type: EvidencePacket
version: "2026-10-20"
statement:
  id: sieve:st/MONDO_0008608-excl-MONDO_0003847
  type: NegativeSubclassStatement
  subject: MONDO:0008608              # Down syndrome
  predicate: {code: rdfs:subClassOf}
  object: MONDO:0003847               # hereditary disease
  negated: true                       # the claim is that it is NOT a subclass
  review_state: VERIFIED
  has_evidence_lines:
    - id: sieve:el/ds-doid-dispute
      type: SieveEvidenceLine
      has_evidence_items: [sieve:ca/doid-14250-isa-630]
      direction_of_evidence_provided: disputes
      score_of_evidence_provided: 0.5
      contributions:
        - id: sieve:act/ds-doid-concordance
          type: InterpretationActivity
          contributor: sieve:agent/concordance-pipeline
          date: "2026-10-20"
          method_type: COMPUTED_CONCORDANCE
          specified_by: [sieve:method/concordance-workflow]
  assertion_decisions:
    - id: sieve:dec/ds-excl-2026
      type: AssertionDecision
      contributor: orcid:0000-0001-5208-3432
      date: "2026-10-20"
      outcome: CONTROVERSIAL
      route: INDIVIDUAL_SIGN_OFF
      inclusion_score: 0.46
      signed_packet_version: "2026-10-20"
prior_claims:
  - id: sieve:ca/doid-14250-isa-630
    type: SubclassStatement           # a prior claim: DOID's own subclass assertion
    subject: DOID:14250               # Disease Ontology: Down syndrome
    predicate: {code: rdfs:subClassOf}
    object: DOID:630                  # genetic disease
    reported_in: [DOID:14250]
    resource: infores:disease-ontology

Disease Ontology places Down syndrome under its genetic disease class, which grounds to Mondo's hereditary disease, so its assertion enters as a disputing line. A curator looked at it and kept the claim, marked controversial. The rest of this page explains the parts.

docs.title: The shape of a packet
docs.text:
graph TD P[EvidencePacketone claim, versioned] --> S[Statementthe claim] S --> L1[Evidence linesupports] S --> L2[Evidence linedisputes] S --> D[Assertion decisionsthe verdicts] S --> O[Originwhere the claim came from] L1 -.-> I1[Item: an OMIM record] L2 -.-> I2[Item: a DOID assertion] P --> I1 P --> I2
  • Statement: the one claim. Its type says which kind of claim it is.
  • Evidence item: one piece of information (a database record, another source's assertion, a passage from a paper, a computed score). Items sit in typed lists on the packet (external_records, prior_claims, text_passages, ...).
  • Evidence line: one judgement that some items bear on the claim, in one direction, with some strength. Lines point at items by id.
  • Assertion decision: whether the claim goes into Mondo, who decided, and on which packet version.
  • Origin: where the claim was copied or cloned from. That is not the same as evidence for it.

Rules, policies, agents and information resources are shared, so they are maintained once in a registry. Each packet still stands on its own: it carries a frozen reference_snapshot of every registry entry it refers to, as of its version.

docs.title: Ten kinds of claim
docs.text:
Each kind of Mondo claim is its own statement class, with its own allowed predicates and its own allowed kinds of evidence:

ID Claim type Example C001 TermExistenceStatement the term exists, is obsolete, is replaced by another C002 DefinitionStatement the term has this definition C003 SynonymStatement "SPOAN syndrome" is an exact synonym C004 SubclassStatement asthma is a respiratory system disorder C005 NegativeSubclassStatement Down syndrome is not a hereditary disease C006 MappingStatement MONDO:0008608 skos:exactMatch ICD10CM:Q90 C007 DiseaseAttributeStatement cystic fibrosis has material basis in CFTR C008 SubsetMembershipStatement the term is in the GARD rare subset C009 MetaclassStatement the term is a grouping class (candidate) C010 ValueSetMembershipStatement the term is an included title of an OMIM record (candidate)

A synonym claim cannot use skos:exactMatch as its predicate, and a definition cannot cite a computed score as evidence. These rules are checked.

docs.title: Two levels of judgement
docs.text:
SIEVE keeps two questions apart:

  1. Does this evidence bear on the claim? That is an evidence line: direction (supports or disputes), strength on a 0-1 scale, and who interpreted it and how (curator, panel, pipeline or AI agent). Lines are never edited. A wrong line is invalidated and replaced, and both stay on record.
  2. Does the claim go into Mondo? That is an assertion decision: outcome (ACCEPTED, REJECTED, CONTROVERSIAL, DEFERRED), the route (individual sign-off, consensus, batch sign-off, or an automated policy that a human approved), and the packet version and score it was given on.

Automated routes can only accept. Anything else goes to a person.

docs.title: Three things that are easy to confuse
docs.text:
Axis Question Where it lives Provenance Where did this come from, and who did what? origin, contributions, resolution chains, retrieval metadata Evidence Does it support or dispute the claim, and how strongly? line direction and strength Data quality Was the evidence read and linked correctly? line and step confidence, with its basis

"This synonym was copied from OMIM in 2019" is provenance. "OMIM still lists it in the 2026 release" is evidence. "The OMIM id was matched to the Mondo term with certainty 1.0" is data quality. A low confidence reduces what a line counts for. It never changes the line's strength.

docs.title: From evidence to a score
docs.text:
The inclusion score S is one number between -1 and +1 saying whether the claim should be in Mondo. Each claim type has a versioned aggregation rule that computes it:

  • each line counts its strength, signed by direction, weighted by the quality of the source and by the confidence it was read correctly;
  • lines that echo the same upstream source form one cluster, and only the strongest line in a cluster counts;
  • the sum is added to a prior for the claim type and proposing channel, and squashed into [-1, 1].

In the published worked examples, cystic fibrosis to CFTR (OMIM, an AI-extracted paper passage and a ClinGen panel) comes out at S ≈ 0.97, and the Down syndrome claim above, with DOID disputing and a curator supporting, at S ≈ 0.46. The score drives the review queue. A person signs it off, and the decision records the S it was given on.

The scoring code for this model is still being written, so the scores in the example packets are illustrative.

docs.title: Checking a packet
docs.text:
uv run linkml-validate -s schema/sieve.yaml -C EvidencePacket my_packet.yaml

then the profile checks in Python (sieve.profile_checks.check_packet). The Workflows page has the details. The review app, ingest and RDF export are being moved to this model and do not work with it yet.

docs.title: Where this comes from
docs.text:
SIEVE is a profile of the SEPIO core information model (Scientific Evidence and Provenance Information Ontology). The core is imported unchanged, and every SIEVE class specialises a core class, so a SIEVE packet is SEPIO data. The profile was built from Mondo's requirements collection; the Requirements Traceability page shows which part of the model answers which requirement.

For every field, see the Data Model.

docs.title: Requirements traceability: Mondo requirements to the SIEVE profile
docs.text: Each requirement from the Mondo requirements collection is assigned to a SEPIO design module and a disposition (requirements/traceability.yaml). The schema elements listed for a requirement are those annotated with its ID in schema/sieve.yaml.

docs.title: SEPIO design modules
docs.text: Module SEPIO core classes Description Statement (claim semantics) (statement) Statement, Proposition, Qualifier What is claimed: SPO(Q) on the Statement, claim-type profiles, negation, and the Statement-level assessment (direction / strength / score in SEPIO's "proposition assessment mode"). Evidence Item (evidence-item) InformationEntity, Document, DataItem, DataSet, StudyResult The information interpreted as evidence: external records, prior claims, documents, computed scores; and the information resources they come from. Evidence Line (interpretation) (evidence-line) EvidenceLine How evidence bears on a claim: evidence lines with direction, strength and score, their validity, and the shortcut links (has_evidence, has_evidence_from_sources). Provenance (activities, contributions, agents, methods) (provenance) Activity, Contribution, Agent, Method Who did what, when, how: interpretation acts, assertion decisions, alignment and retrieval activities, agents with role and trust, rules and policies. Record Metadata (encoding and retrieval of concrete records) (record-metadata) RecordMetadata Provenance of a concrete record rather than its content: where a record was read from, which release, when; how an artefact was serialised. Utilities (utility) Coding, Extension, Qualifier Reusable datatypes (codings, extensions, qualifiers).

docs.title: Statement (claim semantics)
docs.text: Requirement Title Cur → Des Disposition Schema elements Decisions Rationale C001 Term existence / obsoletion – → Y modelled SieveStatement.originTermExistenceStatementTermExistenceStatement.predicateTermExistenceStatement.obsolescence_reasonTermExistenceStatement.scheduled_obsoletion_dateClaimType.TermExistenceStatementTermExistencePredicate D-030, D-039, D-009 TermExistenceStatement. Origin ("cloned from X") is kept apart from evidence ("exactly matches X") via SieveStatement.origin (D-030). Obsolescence reason and replacement are named qualifiers. Subject obsolescence is not stored on mappings; it is read from the term's own existence claim (D-009). C002 Definition – → Y modelled SieveStatement.originDefinitionStatementDefinitionStatement.predicateClaimType.DefinitionStatementDefinitionPredicate D-031, D-020, D-029 DefinitionStatement. Definition dbxrefs are origin with derivation type INSPIRED_BY, not evidence (D-031). Pattern provenance is derived at build time and has no slot (D-020). A definition with no evidence is a WARNING (D-029). C003 Synonym (exact, related, narrow, broad) – → Y modelled SieveStatement.contributionsSynonymStatementSynonymStatement.predicateClaimType.SynonymStatementSynonymPredicate D-031, D-034, D-035 SynonymStatement; scope is the predicate. Synonym support is evidence with last-confirmed dates (D-031). Community endorsement is a contribution with role ENDORSER (D-034, provisional). Synonym types are term metadata and are not modelled (D-035). C004 Subclass placement – → Y modelled SubclassStatementSubclassStatement.predicateClaimType.SubclassStatementSubclassPredicate D-004, D-018, D-025, D-037 SubclassStatement. Reasoning status is deliberately absent (computed, D-018); evidence attaches to entailed axioms like any other. Logical definitions are one statement per intersection_of element with predicate owl:equivalentClass. A full class-expression object is not modelled. C005 Negative subclass (excluded subclass) – → Y modelled SieveStatement.negatedNegativeSubclassStatementNegativeSubclassStatement.negatedClaimType.NegativeSubclassStatementSubclassPredicate D-032, D-033 NegativeSubclassStatement: a SubclassStatement with negated = true (D-032). External records that assert the positive subclass enter as evidence lines with direction = disputes (D-033). C006 Mapping (cross-reference) – → Y modelled SieveStatement.review_stateMappingStatementMappingStatement.predicateMappingStatement.object_obsolete_in_source_versionMappingStatement.preferredMappingStatement.valid_directionClaimType.MappingStatementMappingPredicateMappingDirectionReviewState D-006, D-008, D-010, D-011, D-012, D-014, D-017, D-024 MappingStatement; the predicate comes from the precision code (D-006, D-014). Qualifiers: object_obsolete_in_source_version (D-010), preferred and valid_direction (D-012). Obsolete-to-obsolete mappings and uncoded mappings are WARNING-severity checks (D-011, D-017). Provider authority is an assertion route (D-017, D-064). C007 Disease attribute (definitional) – → Y modelled DiseaseAttributeStatementDiseaseAttributeStatement.predicateClaimType.DiseaseAttributeStatementDiseaseAttributePredicate D-039, D-020 DiseaseAttributeStatement with the Mondo relation set as its predicate value set. The "definitional + pattern-mandated" test (D-039) is computed against the pattern files (D-020), so it gets no stored slot. C008 Subset membership – → Y modelled SieveStatement.contributionsSubsetMembershipStatementSubsetMembershipStatement.predicateClaimType.SubsetMembershipStatementSubsetPredicate D-002, D-035 SubsetMembershipStatement. Provider and stakeholder are contribution roles (D-002). Status-flag subsets are out of scope (D-035). C009 Metaclass / kind of class (CANDIDATE) – → Y modelled MetaclassStatementMetaclassStatement.predicateMetaclassStatement.objectClaimType.MetaclassStatementMetaclassPredicateDiseaseKind D-040 MetaclassStatement (candidate, D-040). Object bound to the kind-of-class vocabulary (grouping / disorder / subtype / susceptibility). C010 Value-set membership (CANDIDATE) – → Y modelled ValueSetMembershipStatementValueSetMembershipStatement.predicateClaimType.ValueSetMembershipStatementValueSetPredicate D-013, D-040 ValueSetMembershipStatement (candidate). Its own predicate sieve:memberOfRecordScope, distinct from SKOS. The interim skos:relatedMatch export is an encoding rule (PROV.ENCODING.METHODS), not a claim predicate. CS.PARENT_SLOT_VALUE Direct Slot–Value on a Parent Record Y → Y out_of_scope – D-041 The plain term-centric consumption form (OBO/JSON without provenance) belongs to Mondo's own model and release, not to this statement profile. CS.NESTED_OBJECT Nested Structured Claim Object within Parent Record Y → Y out_of_scope – D-041, D-042 Primary authoring form (view A) = Mondo's term-centric LinkML model. This profile is view B. Requirement placed on view A: it must carry everything view B needs (origin, contributions, evidence lines with direction and dates, review state, negation). The two are linked by a LinkML-Map transformation (D-042). CS.REIFIED_OBJECT Reified Claim / Statement Object N → Y modelled EvidencePacketSieveStatementSieveStatement.id D-041, D-018 This profile IS view B: identified Statement objects (SieveStatement.id is an identifier), packaged one per EvidencePacket. CS.DIRECT_EDGE Direct Edge / Triple in a Graph Y → Y out_of_scope – D-041, D-065 Release view (OWL / SKOS / SSSOM edges) produced by the release pipeline. Only its meaning-changing export rules are tracked here (PROV.ENCODING.METHODS). CS.OTHER Other N → N not_desired – – No other structure. RCS.FREE_TEXT Human-Readable Claim Text N → M modelled SieveStatement.statement_text – Core Statement.statement_text, optional (M). RCS.STRUCTURED_STATEMENT SPO Semantics on Statement N → Y modelled SieveStatementSieveStatement.subjectSieveStatement.predicateSieveStatement.object D-042 SPO directly on SieveStatement (core subject / predicate / object). subject and object are required; predicate is a Coding bound to a value set per claim type. RCS.STRUCTURED_PROPOSITION SPO Semantics in Nested Proposition N → N negative_constraint SieveStatement.propositionSieveEvidenceLine.target_proposition D-042 No Proposition objects. The core Statement.proposition and EvidenceLine.target_proposition slots are inherited but documented as unused. Concordance and dispute are matched by SPO + negation. RCS.QUALIFIERS Qualifying / Contextual Information N → Y modelled SieveStatement.negatedTermExistenceStatement.obsolescence_reasonTermExistenceStatement.scheduled_obsoletion_dateMappingStatement.object_obsolete_in_source_versionMappingStatement.preferredMappingStatement.valid_directionMappingDirection D-010, D-012, D-013, D-032 Named qualifier slots specialise the core generic qualifier, as the core recommends: object_obsolete_in_source_version, preferred, valid_direction (mappings); obsolescence_reason and scheduled_obsoletion_date (existence). Negation is the profile's Statement-level negated slot. In the core, negated lives only on Proposition, which this profile does not use. PROV.ASSERTION.CONFIDENCE_CATEGORY Assertion Provenance: Confidence Category N → Y modelled SieveStatement.strengthAggregationRule.strength_bandsAssertionDecision.score_band D-062, D-063 Core Statement.strength = the derived band of S, and AssertionDecision.score_band at decision time. No signer-asserted confidence exists in the profile. PROV.ASSERTION.CONFIDENCE_SCORE Assertion Provenance: Confidence Score N → Y modelled SieveStatement.directionSieveStatement.scoreAssertionDecision.inclusion_scoreAssertionDecision.threshold_passed D-063, D-064 Core Statement.score = inclusion score S in [-1, 1]; AssertionDecision.inclusion_score + threshold_passed record S per decision. AI self-confidence is NOT here (line confidence, D-062).

docs.title: Evidence Item
docs.text: Requirement Title Cur → Des Disposition Schema elements Decisions Rationale EI.DATA.EXPERIMENTAL_OBSERVATIONAL Experimental or Observational Data Items N → N not_desired – – Mondo holds no experimental data. EI.DATA.CLINICAL Clinical Measurements or Observations N → N not_desired – – Not used. EI.DATA.STATISTICAL_METRIC Statistical Metrics N → N not_desired – – Not used. docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
Recipes for authoring and checking packets against the SIEVE profile, and for keeping the generated artefacts current. If you are new to the packet shape, read the Primer first; for every field see the Data Model.

Ingest, review and export target the pre-profile model

Sections 1 to 4 work with the current profile. Sections 5 to 8 (ingest into DuckDB, review in the app, RDF / YAML export, ORCID curators) describe the application layer, which still targets the pre-profile model and does not run against current packets. It is being migrated (issues/issue_migrate_app_to_profile.md).

docs.title: 1. Author a packet by hand
docs.text:
A packet is one YAML file per claim: the statement (with its lines, origin and decisions inlined) and the evidence items the lines refer to, in typed lists. Every entity has an id and a type. This synonym claim, copied from OMIM in 2019 and corroborated by the current OMIM release, is adapted from tests/data/profile/valid/c003_spoan_synonym_policy.yaml:

id: sieve:pkt/MONDO_0012297-syn-SPOAN
type: EvidencePacket
version: "2026-10-20"
statement:
  id: sieve:st/MONDO_0012297-syn-SPOAN
  type: SynonymStatement
  subject: MONDO:0012297
  predicate: {code: oboInOwl:hasExactSynonym}
  object: SPOAN syndrome
  review_state: NOT_VERIFIED
  proposing_channel: SOURCE_INGEST
  origin:                              # where the claim came from (not evidence)
    - id: sieve:origin/spoan-omim
      type: OriginEvent
      derivation_type: COPIED_FROM
      source_item: OMIM:609541
      source_label: SPOAN syndrome
      source_release: sieve:release/omim-2019-04-30
      performed_by: [sieve:agent/concordance-pipeline]
      date: "2019-05-02"
  has_evidence_lines:                    # what corroborates it now
    - id: sieve:el/spoan-omim
      type: SieveEvidenceLine
      has_evidence_items: [sieve:ca/omim-609541-syn]
      direction_of_evidence_provided: supports
      strength_of_evidence_provided: strong
      score_of_evidence_provided: 0.9
      computed_by_rule: sieve:rule/synonym-v1.1
      confidence: 1.0
      confidence_basis: DETERMINISTIC
      last_confirmed: "2026-10-01"
      last_confirmed_against: sieve:release/omim-2026-10-01
      contributions:
        - id: sieve:act/spoan-omim
          type: InterpretationActivity
          contributor: sieve:agent/concordance-pipeline
          date: "2026-10-20"
          method_type: COMPUTED_CONCORDANCE
          specified_by: [sieve:method/concordance-workflow]
          read_coverage: STRUCTURED_RECORD
prior_claims:
  - id: sieve:ca/omim-609541-syn
    type: SynonymStatement
    subject: OMIM:609541
    predicate: {code: oboInOwl:hasExactSynonym}
    object: SPOAN syndrome
    reported_in: [OMIM:609541]
    resource: infores:omim
external_records:
  - id: OMIM:609541
    type: ExternalRecord
    resource: infores:omim
    generation_context:
      - {code: "sieve:basis_unknown"}
    record_metadata:
      retrieved_from: infores:omim
      source_release: sieve:release/omim-2026-10-01
      retrieval_date: "2026-10-02"

Notes:

  • Pick the statement type for the claim (SynonymStatement, MappingStatement, ...); it fixes which predicates and which item classes are allowed.
  • Lines refer to items by id. Each item goes in the list for its class.
  • Rules, releases, agents and methods (sieve:rule/..., sieve:release/..., infores:...) are ids in a SieveRegistry; see tests/data/profile/registry.yaml.
  • A new claim usually has no assertion_decisions yet. The full test file adds the policy-based acceptance and the resolution chain for the OMIM id.
  • Quote dates, so linkml-validate reads them as strings.

docs.title: 2. Validate
docs.text:
Two steps. First the schema, with linkml-validate:

uv run linkml-validate -s schema/sieve.yaml -C EvidencePacket inbox/my_packet.yaml
uv run linkml-validate -s schema/sieve.yaml -C SieveRegistry  registry.yaml

It prints No issues found, or one [ERROR] line per problem, and exits non-zero on errors. A statement error inside a packet is reported as "not valid under any of the given schemas in /statement", because the statement can be any claim type. To see the specific reason, validate the statement on its own against its class (for example -C SynonymStatement on a file holding only the statement).

Then the profile checks:

import yaml
from sieve.profile_checks import check_packet

packet = yaml.safe_load(open("inbox/my_packet.yaml"))
for issue in check_packet(packet):
    print(issue.severity, issue.code, issue.requirement, issue.message)

An empty list means the packet passes. ERRORs are profile violations; WARNINGs are states that need a person (for example a definition with no evidence and no origin). Pass obsolete_terms={...} to flag obsolete-to-obsolete mappings.

docs.title: 3. Use the generated Pydantic model
docs.text:
import yaml
from sieve.datamodel import EvidencePacket

packet = EvidencePacket.model_validate(yaml.safe_load(open("inbox/my_packet.yaml")))
type(packet.statement).__name__     # "SynonymStatement"
packet.statement.has_evidence_lines[0].direction_of_evidence_provided

The type designators select the concrete classes, so no custom loader is needed.

docs.title: 4. Keep generated artefacts current
docs.text:
After editing schema/sieve.yaml or requirements/traceability.yaml:

just gen-pydantic          # regenerate src/sieve/datamodel/sieve_models.py
just gen-traceability      # regenerate docs/requirements-traceability.md
just gen-docs              # regenerate the schema reference in docs/elements/

When the Mondo requirements workbook changes, re-extract the TSV. The default path assumes sepio-linkml is checked out next to this repository:

just extract-requirements
just extract-requirements /path/to/Mondo_Requirements_Collection_Forms.xlsx

tests/test_profile_schema.py and tests/test_traceability.py fail if the checked-in model or traceability page is stale, if a requirement has no trace entry, or if an annotated requirement ID does not exist.

docs.title: 5. Ingest into DuckDB (pre-profile)
docs.text:
sieve ingest loaded every *.yaml / *.yml packet under a directory into DuckDB (default data/sieve.duckdb), stored its JSON, computed its Net Evidence Ratio, and reported per-file errors without aborting the batch:

sieve ingest -I inbox/examples/ --db data/sieve.duckdb

Re-ingesting a packet with an existing id overwrote it. The command currently fails at import.

docs.title: 6. Review in the app (pre-profile)
docs.text:
sieve run launches the Streamlit app with Dashboard, Review Queue, Ingest and Export pages. An authorised curator (ORCID login, manual ORCID entry, or SIEVE_DEV_MODE=true) could accept or reject individual items and record an Accept / Reject / Controversial decision, which wrote a CurationDecision and set the packet's status.

In the profile these become a LineStatusChange on a line, an AssertionDecision with route INDIVIDUAL_SIGN_OFF, and the statement's review_state.

docs.title: 7. Export to RDF and YAML (pre-profile)
docs.text:
sieve export read packet files and emitted RDF (rdf/turtle/ttl, xml, n3, nt) or combined YAML:

sieve export -I exports/accepted/ -O rdf -o accepted.ttl
sieve export -I packets/ -O yaml -o combined.yaml

Each decided packet became an owl:Axiom annotation of the statement, linked back to the packet via SEPIO:0000124. Undecided packets were skipped with a warning. See cli.md for the options.

docs.title: 8. ORCID auth and curators
docs.text:
Who may record decisions in the app is controlled by ORCID identity plus a curators.yaml allow-list (path overridable via CURATORS_FILE), matched by ORCID with or without the orcid: prefix:

curators:
  - orcid: "0000-0001-2345-6789"
    name: "Dr. Jane Smith"
    role: admin
  - orcid: "0000-0002-3456-7890"
    name: "Dr. John Doe"
    role: curator

Modes: ORCID OAuth (ORCID_CLIENT_ID / ORCID_CLIENT_SECRET, optionally ORCID_REDIRECT_URI, ORCID_SANDBOX), manual ORCID entry when OAuth is not configured, and SIEVE_DEV_MODE=true, which bypasses auth. The file is re-read roughly once a minute. See ORCID Setup.

docs.title: SIEVE - a SEPIO profile for evidence-based curation of Mondo claims
docs.text:
SIEVE is a profile of the SEPIO core information model (schema/sepio_core.yaml, imported unchanged). Every class here specialises a SEPIO core class. Every inherited slot keeps or narrows its core range. Nothing in the core is redefined.

The profile is driven by the Mondo requirements collection (requirements/mondo_requirements.tsv). Each class, slot, enum and permissible value that realises a requirement carries it in annotations.requirements (space-separated requirement IDs) and, where a modelling decision lies behind it, in annotations.decisions (Mondo decision-log IDs). requirements/traceability.yaml assigns every requirement to a SEPIO design module and a disposition. tests/test_traceability.py keeps both sides consistent.

Shape of the data: one EvidencePacket per claim. It holds one claim-type Statement (view B of D-041: identified, reified statement objects), the evidence items its lines refer to, and a version. Rules, policies, agents and information resources are shared reference data held in a SieveRegistry.

Profile conventions: names follow the core's camelCase. Narrowed core slots are declared via slot_usage. Value sets for Coding-typed core slots are declared as bindings and enforced by sieve.profile_checks, because linkml-validate does not enforce bindings.

URI: https://w3id.org/sieve

Name: sieve

docs.title: Comments
docs.text: • Activities relevant to scientific knowledge generation, and include things like observations of the natural world, designing and performing experiments, data analysis and transformation, publishing research results, data curation and interpretation, and assessment and care of patients in clinical settings. These activities may produce information that gets encoded in sharable artifacts which are used to generate scientific knowledge. Agents can play different types of roles in the generation and use of such artifacts.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
• Agents perform activities and make contributions to entities. An agent can be an individual person, an organization of multiple individuals acting together, or a computational agent such as a software program or automated pipeline.
  • Agents can belong to organizations, and act on behalf or in the context of an organizational affiliation when contributing to an entity. For example, curators generating these variant pathogenicity interpretations may do so in the context of their work with the ClinGen organization, which provides administrative, technical, and funding support for their contributions.

      how data were generated, or an evidence interpretation guideline that describes
      steps taken to interpret data in making a variant pathogenicity classification.

      (e.g. the specific electron microscopy method described in https://doi.org/10.1002/
      cpz1.1045) - as opposed to reporting a *type* of method applied (e.g. "Transmission
      Electron Microscopy").

    required: false

    name: sources
    description: A document or other informtion resource in which the information
      entity, or evidence supporting it, is reported.
    comments:
    - This attribute is more general than InformationEntity.reportedIn (which is used
      to references a Docuement that directly reports the infrormation), and Statement.hasEvidenceFromSources
      (which is used to reference resources that provided evidence used to generate
      the knowledge expressed in a Statement). It can be used to cover both cases,
      in situations where a data provider does not know which is the case, or does
      not wish to make the distinction.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    alias: sources
    owner: AggregationRule
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  information_quality:
    name: information_quality
    description: A qualitative term indicating the scientific rigor or reliability
      with which the information was generated/collected.
    comments:
    - This is typically based on the quality of design and execution of the study
      or curation activity that generated it (e.g. were relevant controls assessed
      to show instruments were working, were all samples taken care of and handled
      identically, are methods sound and well documented, etc.).
    - The quality of information is intrinsic to the information itself, and not to
      a particular application of the information (e.g. as evidence for making an
      Assertion)
    - The quality of information is one factor that goes into the confidence we have
      in the information''s veracity (i.e. that it is an accurate reflection of reality
      it intends to measure or describe). Other factors informing confidence may include
      who did it (we may just not trust some Agents), when (if data created 500 years
      ago, we may have less confidence in it), and for Assertions, the relevance and
      abundance of supporting evidence.
    - Implementers should define a relevant source of codes or terms to use here,
      based on the needs of the domain or application.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model

    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:informationQuality
    alias: information_quality
    owner: AggregationRule
    domain_of:

    range: Coding
    required: false
    multivalued: false

      as encoded/serialized in a particular data set or object (as opposed to provenance
      about the abstract information content the encoding carries).
    comments:
    - This attribute holds a structured RecordMetadata objects, which can be used

      information such as versioning and lifecycle status.

    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: RecordMetadata
    required: false
    multivalued: false

    description: The 'logical' identifier of the entity in the system of record, e.g.
      a UUID.  This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally
      unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference one object
      from another.
    comments:
    - Note that it is common for implementers to create their own internal logical
      ids - typically a serially or randomly generated value like a UUID that is assigned
      to the data object as it is created in a system. But an implementer may choose
      to reuse an existing, globally unique id from an external system or authority
      for this purpose (e.g. an HGNC id for a Gene object) - as long as it is unique
      within the implementing system, and can be used to reference the identified
      object in this context.

    identifier: true

    domain_of:

    range: string
    required: true
    multivalued: false
  identifiers:
    name: identifiers
    description: A globally-unique 'business' identifier or accession number for the
      real-world entity represented by a data object. These are typically assigned
      by an external system or authority, and used to connect entities and share content
      across different systems.
    comments:
    - Preferred values for this attribute are CURIEs or URIs - so the system that
      provisioned the identifier is clear.
    - A given real world entity - e.g. a genetic variant - may have many business
      identifiers defined by different systems, which can be captured in the "identifiers"
      property to indicate that they represent the same thing.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    alias: identifiers
    owner: AggregationRule
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  type:
    name: type
    description: The name of the class that is instantiated by a data object representing
      the Entity.
    comments:
    - MUST be the label of a concrete class from the data model.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    designates_type: true
    alias: type
    owner: AggregationRule
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: string
    required: true
    multivalued: false
  label:
    name: label
    description: A primary name for the Entity.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft

    alias: label
    owner: AggregationRule
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    - Coding

    required: false
    multivalued: false
  alternative_labels:
    name: alternative_labels
    description: Alternative name(s) for the Entity.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:alternativeLabels
    alias: alternative_labels
    owner: AggregationRule
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  description:
    name: description
    description: A free text description of the Entity.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    alias: description
    owner: AggregationRule
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  extensions:
    name: extensions
    description: A list of extensions to the Entity, that allow for capture of information
      not directly supported by elements defined in the model.
    comments:
    - Extension objects have a key-value data structure that allows definition of
      custom fields in the data itself. Extensions are not expected to be natively

      between systems.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    alias: extensions
    owner: AggregationRule
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: Extension

One extraction, translation, grounding or normalisation step. It records its input and output value, method, agent, rules applied, quality category, confidence with basis, and review status. Reviewing a step answers "did the machine read and link correctly?". That is separate from reviewing the claim.

docs.title: Class: AssertionDecision
docs.text:
The overall decision that puts a claim into Mondo (or keeps it out). It is made over all lines and recorded with the score, rule and packet version it was given on. Every claim rests on a human decision: per claim (sign-off, consensus, batch) or per policy (delegated, provider authority). Automated routes can only accept.

docs.title: Class: BatchSignOff
docs.text:
A one-off curator approval of a filtered result set, with banded review depth. Distinct from a standing policy. The filter is stored so it can be re-run, and the result set is frozen with packet versions, so a batch can be queried and revoked as a unit.

    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    alias: value
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - LevelAssignment
    - DataItem
    - Qualifier
    - Expression
    - Extension
    range: string
    required: true
    multivalued: false
  unit:
    name: unit
    description: A unit of measure for the value (e.g. meters, grams, fluorescent
      units, seconds, mg/ml, etc.)
    comments:
    - Implementers should define a relevant source or specific set of unit terms/codes
      to use here based on the needs of the domain or application.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    alias: unit
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - DataItem
    range: Coding
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  variability_measures:
    name: variability_measures
    description: A statistical score describing the variability inherent in a data
      item representing a statistical summary of a set of observations/measurements
      (e.g. the standard deviation associated with a statistical mean calculated across
      several experimental replicates).
    comments:
    - Examples of statistical measures of variability include an Interquartile Range,
      Variance, Standard Deviation, Standard Error. The type of variability measure
      used here represents should be reported in the DataItem instance created to
      represent it.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:variabilityMeasures
    alias: variability_measures
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - DataItem
    range: DataItem
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  confidence_interval:
    name: confidence_interval
    description: A measure of the probability that a parameter of interest will fall
      within a defined range of values around a mean or other statistical calculation.
    comments:
    - Confidence intervals reflect the degree of uncertainty in a sampling method.
      They may be bounded on one or both sides, and are  computed for a designated
      confidence level (most often 95% or 99%.. For example, a Hazard Ratio of 0.47
      might have a 95% confidence interval between 0.42 and 0.55, with a p-value of
      = 0.001.
    - The DataItem used to represent a confidence interval will indicate what type
      of interval is reported (e.g. ''95% CI''), and will contain separate componentDataItems
      representing the upper and lower bounds of the interval (e.g. ''0.42'' and ''0.55'').'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:confidenceInterval
    alias: confidence_interval
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - DataItem
    range: DataItem
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  component_data_item:
    name: component_data_item
    description: A more foundational data item that is a logical component of a compound
      data item.
    comments:
    - Examples of 'compound' data items with component parts include a confidence
      interval, which is comprised of data items representing its lower and upper
      bounds,  or a blood pressure reading, which is comprised of separate systolic
      and diastolic measurements.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:componentDataItem
    alias: component_data_item
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - DataItem
    range: DataItem
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  is_about:
    name: is_about
    description: An entity or concept in the world that the information entity describes/is
      about.
    comments:
    - e.g. In the context of a Statement object, this attribute may be used to indicate
      entities/concepts it is about, in lieu of providing a more precise description
      of what the Statement asserts to be true using subject, predicate, object, and
      qualifier properties. e.g. the Statement that "BRCA2 c.8023A>G is pathogenic
      for Breast Cancer" might be annotated to be about the variant 'BRCA2 c.8023A>G',
      and the disease 'Breast Cancer'.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:isAbout
    alias: is_about
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  contributions:
    name: contributions
    description: Specific actions taken by an Agent toward the creation, modification,
      validation, or deprecation of an Information Entity.
    comments:
    - This attribute holds one or more Contribution objects, which provide structured
      descriptions of a contribution made to the Information Entity by a particular
      agent.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    alias: contributions
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    - RecordMetadata
    range: Contribution
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  date_authored:
    name: date_authored
    description: Indicates when the information content expressed in the Information
      Entity was generated.
    comments:
    - The term 'authored' as used in the model refers to the generation of 'information
      content' in the abstract  sense, as opposed to a concrete encoding of this information
      in a specific language or format. e.g. for a Statement, this attribute captures
      when the information content expressed in the Statement was first generated
      by an agent.  Information about when a particular concrete encoding of this
      information was created (e.g. as row in a table, or object in a json document)
      would live in a RecordMetadata object attached to the Information Entity).
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:dateAuthored
    alias: date_authored
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  specified_by:
    name: specified_by
    description: The method / tool that computed the score.
    comments:
    - Examples - an experimental protocol or data analysis specification that describe
      how data were generated, or an evidence interpretation guideline that describes
      steps taken to interpret data in making a variant pathogenicity classification.
    - Note that this attribute captures specific *instances* of specifications/methods
      (e.g. the specific electron microscopy method described in https://doi.org/10.1002/
      cpz1.1045) - as opposed to reporting a *type* of method applied (e.g. "Transmission
      Electron Microscopy").
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:specifiedBy
    alias: specified_by
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    - Activity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  supporting_methods:
    name: supporting_methods
    description: Specific methods that were executed to directly or indirectly support
      creation of the Information Entity.
    comments:
    - These may include methods that directly produced the Information Entity, or
      upstream/accessory methods that indirectly support creation of the Information
      Entity - e.g. methods used to produce data that was interpreted as evidence
      to generate a Statement of knowledge.
    - This field captures terms representing specific INSTANCES of methods applied,
      vs the 'supportingMethodTypes' attribute which captures TYPES of methods used.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:supportingMethods
    alias: supporting_methods
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  supporting_method_types:
    name: supporting_method_types
    description: Types of methodological approaches that were executed to directly
      or indirectly support creation of the Information Entity.
    comments:
    - This field captures terms representing TYPES of methods applied, vs the 'specifiedBy'
      or'supportingMethods' attributes which capture specific INSTANCES of methods
      used. These may include types of methods that directly produced the Information
      Entity, or upstream/accessory methods that indirectly support creation of the
      Information Entity
    - Implementers should define a relevant source or set of method type codes/terms
      to use here, based on the needs of the domain or application.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:supportingMethodTypes
    alias: supporting_method_types
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: Coding
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  derived_from:
    name: derived_from
    description: Another Information Entity from which this Information Entity is
      derived, in whole or in part.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:derivedFrom
    alias: derived_from
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: InformationEntity
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  reported_in:
    name: reported_in
    description: A document in which the Information Entity is reported.
    comments:
    - This attribute is used specifically to reference documents/publications where
      the Information Entity is expressed or reported.  For a Statement, this might
      be a publication where the authors express the statement in text. For a Data
      Item, this might be a publication with a table or figure that reports the value
      of the  data.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:reportedIn
    alias: reported_in
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  sources:
    name: sources
    description: A document or other informtion resource in which the information
      entity, or evidence supporting it, is reported.
    comments:
    - This attribute is more general than InformationEntity.reportedIn (which is used
      to references a Docuement that directly reports the infrormation), and Statement.hasEvidenceFromSources
      (which is used to reference resources that provided evidence used to generate
      the knowledge expressed in a Statement). It can be used to cover both cases,
      in situations where a data provider does not know which is the case, or does
      not wish to make the distinction.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    alias: sources
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  information_quality:
    name: information_quality
    description: A qualitative term indicating the scientific rigor or reliability
      with which the information was generated/collected.
    comments:
    - This is typically based on the quality of design and execution of the study
      or curation activity that generated it (e.g. were relevant controls assessed
      to show instruments were working, were all samples taken care of and handled
      identically, are methods sound and well documented, etc.).
    - The quality of information is intrinsic to the information itself, and not to
      a particular application of the information (e.g. as evidence for making an
      Assertion)
    - The quality of information is one factor that goes into the confidence we have
      in the information''s veracity (i.e. that it is an accurate reflection of reality
      it intends to measure or describe). Other factors informing confidence may include
      who did it (we may just not trust some Agents), when (if data created 500 years
      ago, we may have less confidence in it), and for Assertions, the relevance and
      abundance of supporting evidence.
    - Implementers should define a relevant source of codes or terms to use here,
      based on the needs of the domain or application.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:informationQuality
    alias: information_quality
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: Coding
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  record_metadata:
    name: record_metadata
    description: Provenance metadata about a specific concrete record of information
      as encoded/serialized in a particular data set or object (as opposed to provenance
      about the abstract information content the encoding carries).
    comments:
    - This attribute holds a structured RecordMetadata objects, which can be used
      to capture when, how, and by whom a record serialization was generated or modified;
      what upstream resources it was derived or retrieved from; and record-level administrative
      information such as versioning and lifecycle status.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:recordMetadata
    alias: record_metadata
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: RecordMetadata
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  identifiers:
    name: identifiers
    description: A globally-unique 'business' identifier or accession number for the
      real-world entity represented by a data object. These are typically assigned
      by an external system or authority, and used to connect entities and share content
      across different systems.
    comments:
    - Preferred values for this attribute are CURIEs or URIs - so the system that
      provisioned the identifier is clear.
    - A given real world entity - e.g. a genetic variant - may have many business
      identifiers defined by different systems, which can be captured in the "identifiers"
      property to indicate that they represent the same thing.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    alias: identifiers
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  type:
    name: type
    description: The name of the class that is instantiated by a data object representing
      the Entity.
    comments:
    - MUST be the label of a concrete class from the data model.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    designates_type: true
    alias: type
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: string
    required: true
    multivalued: false
  label:
    name: label
    description: A primary name for the Entity.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    alias: label
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    - Coding
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  alternative_labels:
    name: alternative_labels
    description: Alternative name(s) for the Entity.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:alternativeLabels
    alias: alternative_labels
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  description:
    name: description
    description: A free text description of the Entity.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    alias: description
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  extensions:
    name: extensions
    description: A list of extensions to the Entity, that allow for capture of information
      not directly supported by elements defined in the model.
    comments:
    - Extension objects have a key-value data structure that allows definition of
      custom fields in the data itself. Extensions are not expected to be natively
      understood, but may be used for pre-negotiated exchange of message attributes
      between systems.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    alias: extensions
    owner: ComputationalScore
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: Extension
    required: false
    multivalued: true

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
• Contributions are used to organize information about when, where, how (e.g. what roles were played), and on whose behalf these actions were performed.
  • The scope of a Contribution instance includes only the actions of a single agent in contributing to a single artifact, which may be performed in one continuous effort, or several discontinuous sessions of work. The agent can be an individual person, a software agent, or a group or organization of individuals acting together.'

name: Contribution
description: An action or actions taken by a particular agent in the creation, modification,
  assessment, or deprecation of some entity (e.g. a Statement, Evidence Line, DataSet,
  Publication, etc.).
title: Contribution
comments:
- Contributions are used to organize information about when, where, how (e.g. what
  roles were played), and on whose behalf these actions were performed.
- The scope of a Contribution instance includes only the actions of a single agent
  in contributing to a single artifact, which may be performed in one continuous effort,
  or several discontinuous sessions of work.  The agent can be an individual person,
  a software agent, or a group or organization of individuals acting together.'
from_schema: https://w3id.org/sieve
status: Draft
is_a: Activity
attributes:
  contributor:
    name: contributor
    description: The Agent that made the contribution.
    comments:
    - Note that this must be a single agent (which can be a Person, or an Organization).  If
      multiple Agents contributed to an entity, a separate Contribution instances
      MUST be created for each.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    domain_of:
    - Contribution
    range: Agent
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  activity_type:
    name: activity_type
    description: The specific type of activity performed or role played by an agent
      in making the contribution (e.g. for a publication, agents may contribute as
      a primary author, editor, figure designer, data generator, etc. . Values of
      this property may be framed as activities or as contribution roles (e.g. using
      terms from the Contribution Role Ontology (CRO)).
    comments:
    - Each implementation can define terms for the specific types of activities relevant
      to their use case/application. \n- Note that if the same Agent performed multiple
      types of activities in contributing to some artifact, they may all be captured
      in a single Contribution object. However, if data creators want to provide metadata
      specific to each activity (e.g. when or how each was performed), then a separate
      Contribution object should be created for each activity.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000

    domain_of:
    - Contribution
    range: Coding
    required: false
    multivalued: true

    - Contribution
    range: InformationEntity

    multivalued: false

docs.title: Direct
docs.text:
name: DataItem
description: An Information Entity representing an individual piece of data, generated
  or acquired through methods which reliably produce truthful information about something.
title: Data Item
comments:
- Examples include raw observations or measurements such as an allele count, or patient's
  weight, derived calculations such as frequency or mean, and computed statistical
  scores/metrics such as p-values and z-scores.
from_schema: https://w3id.org/sieve
status: Informative
is_a: InformationEntity
attributes:
  subtype:
    name: subtype
    description: A specific type of data the DataItem instance represents (e.g. a
      'specimen count', a 'patient weight', an 'allele frequency', a 'p-value')
    comments:
    - This attribute can be used to report a specific type for the DataItem, in cases
      where a model does not define DataItem subclasses for this purpose.  Implementers
      can define their own set of data item type codes/terms, to match the needs of
      the domain or application.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    domain_of:
    - Method
    - Document
    - DataItem
    - DataSet
    - Activity
    - Agent
    - EvidenceLine
    range: Coding
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  value:
    name: value
    description: The value of the data item (could be quantitative or qualitative
      depending on the type of data item).
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    domain_of:
    - LevelAssignment
    - DataItem
    - Qualifier
    - Expression
    - Extension
    range: string
    required: true
    multivalued: false
  unit:
    name: unit
    description: A unit of measure for the value (e.g. meters, grams, fluorescent
      units, seconds, mg/ml, etc.)
    comments:
    - Implementers should define a relevant source or specific set of unit terms/codes
      to use here based on the needs of the domain or application.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    domain_of:
    - DataItem
    range: Coding
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  variability_measures:
    name: variability_measures
    description: A statistical score describing the variability inherent in a data
      item representing a statistical summary of a set of observations/measurements
      (e.g. the standard deviation associated with a statistical mean calculated across
      several experimental replicates).
    comments:
    - Examples of statistical measures of variability include an Interquartile Range,
      Variance, Standard Deviation, Standard Error. The type of variability measure
      used here represents should be reported in the DataItem instance created to
      represent it.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:variabilityMeasures
    domain_of:
    - DataItem
    range: DataItem
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  confidence_interval:
    name: confidence_interval
    description: A measure of the probability that a parameter of interest will fall
      within a defined range of values around a mean or other statistical calculation.
    comments:
    - Confidence intervals reflect the degree of uncertainty in a sampling method.
      They may be bounded on one or both sides, and are  computed for a designated
      confidence level (most often 95% or 99%.. For example, a Hazard Ratio of 0.47
      might have a 95% confidence interval between 0.42 and 0.55, with a p-value of
      = 0.001.
    - The DataItem used to represent a confidence interval will indicate what type
      of interval is reported (e.g. ''95% CI''), and will contain separate componentDataItems
      representing the upper and lower bounds of the interval (e.g. ''0.42'' and ''0.55'').'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:confidenceInterval
    domain_of:
    - DataItem
    range: DataItem
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  component_data_item:
    name: component_data_item
    description: A more foundational data item that is a logical component of a compound
      data item.
    comments:
    - Examples of 'compound' data items with component parts include a confidence
      interval, which is comprised of data items representing its lower and upper
      bounds,  or a blood pressure reading, which is comprised of separate systolic
      and diastolic measurements.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:componentDataItem
    domain_of:
    - DataItem
    range: DataItem
    required: false
    multivalued: true

  is_about:

    comments:

      Entity was generated.

      to creation of the Information Entity.
    comments:
    - Examples - an experimental protocol or data analysis specification that describe
      how data were generated, or an evidence interpretation guideline that describes
      steps taken to interpret data in making a variant pathogenicity classification.
    - Note that this attribute captures specific *instances* of specifications/methods
      (e.g. the specific electron microscopy method described in https://doi.org/10.1002/
      cpz1.1045) - as opposed to reporting a *type* of method applied (e.g. "Transmission
      Electron Microscopy").
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:specifiedBy
    alias: specified_by
    owner: DataItem
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    - Activity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true

      creation of the Information Entity.
    comments:
    - These may include methods that directly produced the Information Entity, or
      upstream/accessory methods that indirectly support creation of the Information
      Entity - e.g. methods used to produce data that was interpreted as evidence
      to generate a Statement of knowledge.
    - This field captures terms representing specific INSTANCES of methods applied,
      vs the 'supportingMethodTypes' attribute which captures TYPES of methods used.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative

    slot_uri: sepio-model:supportingMethods

    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true

      or indirectly support creation of the Information Entity.
    comments:
    - This field captures terms representing TYPES of methods applied, vs the 'specifiedBy'
      or'supportingMethods' attributes which capture specific INSTANCES of methods

    - Implementers should define a relevant source or set of method type codes/terms

    comments:
    - This attribute is used specifically to reference documents/publications where
      the Information Entity is expressed or reported.  For a Statement, this might
      be a publication where the authors express the statement in text. For a Data
      Item, this might be a publication with a table or figure that reports the value

      entity, or evidence supporting it, is reported.
    comments:
    - This attribute is more general than InformationEntity.reportedIn (which is used
      to references a Docuement that directly reports the infrormation), and Statement.hasEvidenceFromSources
      (which is used to reference resources that provided evidence used to generate
      the knowledge expressed in a Statement). It can be used to cover both cases,
      in situations where a data provider does not know which is the case, or does
      not wish to make the distinction.

    status: Draft
    rank: 1000

    owner: DataItem
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  information_quality:
    name: information_quality
    description: A qualitative term indicating the scientific rigor or reliability
      with which the information was generated/collected.
    comments:
    - This is typically based on the quality of design and execution of the study
      or curation activity that generated it (e.g. were relevant controls assessed
      to show instruments were working, were all samples taken care of and handled
      identically, are methods sound and well documented, etc.).
    - The quality of information is intrinsic to the information itself, and not to
      a particular application of the information (e.g. as evidence for making an
      Assertion)

      in the information''s veracity (i.e. that it is an accurate reflection of reality
      it intends to measure or describe). Other factors informing confidence may include
      who did it (we may just not trust some Agents), when (if data created 500 years
      ago, we may have less confidence in it), and for Assertions, the relevance and
      abundance of supporting evidence.
    - Implementers should define a relevant source of codes or terms to use here,
      based on the needs of the domain or application.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000

docs.text:
name: DataSet
description: A collection of related data items or records that are organized together
  in a common format or structure, to enable their computational manipulation as a
  unit.
title: Data Set
comments:
- Instances of this class represent a *specific version* of a given dataset. Examples
  include the  gnomAD version 3.1.2 dataset carrying allele population frequencies,
  or a specific version of a VCF file that describes variations observed in a particular
  patient and various annotations made on them, or a SIFT dataset of computational
  predictions functional impact for a set of variants.
from_schema: https://w3id.org/sieve
status: Draft
is_a: InformationEntity
attributes:
  subtype:
    name: subtype
    description: A specific type of data set the DataSet instance represents (e.g.
      a 'clinical data set', a 'sequencing data set', a 'gene expression data set',
      a 'genome annotation data set').
    comments:
    - This attribute can be used to report a specific type for the DataSet, in cases
      where a model does not define DataSet subclasses for this purpose.  Implementers
      can define their own set of data set type codes/terms, to match the needs of
      the domain or application.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    domain_of:
    - Method
    - Document
    - DataItem
    - DataSet
    - Activity
    - Agent
    - EvidenceLine
    range: Coding
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  release_date:
    name: release_date
    description: Indicates when a version of a DataSet was formally released.
    comments:
    - This attribute may apply to version and distribution-level DataSet representations.
      It refers to when the data set was released, which may be different than the
      data set was generated.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:releaseDate
    domain_of:
    - DataSet
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  version:
    name: version
    description: The version of the DataSet, as assigned by its creator.
    comments:
    - This property can capture version information for resources such as data sets
      and documents that get published and released as a unit for community use. These
      may go through rounds of revisions that add or modify content, but don't change
      the identity of the resource. Use this attribute in cases where version is not
      reflected in an identifier associated with the data set
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    domain_of:
    - SieveMethod
    - DataSet
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: false
  license:
    name: license
    description: A specific license that dictates legal permissions for how a data
      set can be used (by whom, where, for what purposes, with what additional requirements,
      etc.).
    comments:
    - Where possible, provide a URL pointing to the license or a description of it
      (e.g. "https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"). Otherwise, provide a
      free-text name or description of the license (e.g. "CC-BY").
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    domain_of:
    - Document
    - DataSet
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: false

docs.title: Class: DecisionPolicy
docs.text:
A human-authored, human-approved decision procedure that an automated system applies to accept claims: scope, thresholds, rule versions. It can only accept. Everything else goes to the human queue. Provider authority (GARD, NORD, NANDO xrefs) is one such policy.

    range: Contribution

      how data were generated, or an evidence interpretation guideline that describes
      steps taken to interpret data in making a variant pathogenicity classification.

      (e.g. the specific electron microscopy method described in https://doi.org/10.1002/
      cpz1.1045) - as opposed to reporting a *type* of method applied (e.g. "Transmission

    name: sources
    description: A document or other informtion resource in which the information
      entity, or evidence supporting it, is reported.
    comments:
    - This attribute is more general than InformationEntity.reportedIn (which is used
      to references a Docuement that directly reports the infrormation), and Statement.hasEvidenceFromSources
      (which is used to reference resources that provided evidence used to generate
      the knowledge expressed in a Statement). It can be used to cover both cases,
      in situations where a data provider does not know which is the case, or does
      not wish to make the distinction.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    alias: sources
    owner: DecisionPolicy
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true
  information_quality:
    name: information_quality
    description: A qualitative term indicating the scientific rigor or reliability
      with which the information was generated/collected.
    comments:
    - This is typically based on the quality of design and execution of the study
      or curation activity that generated it (e.g. were relevant controls assessed
      to show instruments were working, were all samples taken care of and handled
      identically, are methods sound and well documented, etc.).
    - The quality of information is intrinsic to the information itself, and not to
      a particular application of the information (e.g. as evidence for making an
      Assertion)
    - The quality of information is one factor that goes into the confidence we have
      in the information''s veracity (i.e. that it is an accurate reflection of reality
      it intends to measure or describe). Other factors informing confidence may include
      who did it (we may just not trust some Agents), when (if data created 500 years
      ago, we may have less confidence in it), and for Assertions, the relevance and
      abundance of supporting evidence.
    - Implementers should define a relevant source of codes or terms to use here,
      based on the needs of the domain or application.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model

    rank: 1000
    slot_uri: sepio-model:informationQuality
    alias: information_quality
    owner: DecisionPolicy
    domain_of:
    - InformationEntity
    range: Coding
    required: false
    multivalued: false

      as encoded/serialized in a particular data set or object (as opposed to provenance
      about the abstract information content the encoding carries).

      a UUID.  This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally
      unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference one object
      from another.
    comments:
    - Note that it is common for implementers to create their own internal logical
      ids - typically a serially or randomly generated value like a UUID that is assigned
      to the data object as it is created in a system. But an implementer may choose
      to reuse an existing, globally unique id from an external system or authority
      for this purpose (e.g. an HGNC id for a Gene object) - as long as it is unique
      within the implementing system, and can be used to reference the identified
      object in this context.

    identifier: true
    alias: id
    owner: DecisionPolicy

    required: true
    multivalued: false

      real-world entity represented by a data object. These are typically assigned
      by an external system or authority, and used to connect entities and share content
      across different systems.
    comments:
    - Preferred values for this attribute are CURIEs or URIs - so the system that
      provisioned the identifier is clear.
    - A given real world entity - e.g. a genetic variant - may have many business
      identifiers defined by different systems, which can be captured in the "identifiers"
      property to indicate that they represent the same thing.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Informative
    rank: 1000
    alias: identifiers
    owner: DecisionPolicy
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: string
    required: false
    multivalued: true

    name: type
    description: The name of the class that is instantiated by a data object representing
      the Entity.
    comments:
    - MUST be the label of a concrete class from the data model.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/sepio-model
    status: Draft
    rank: 1000
    designates_type: true
    alias: type
    owner: DecisionPolicy
    domain_of:
    - Entity
    range: string
    required: true

      in the domain - ideally using terms from community ontologies or terminologies.

      value set might include terms from the GENO ontology defining  'pathogenic for
      condition', 'benign for condition', and 'uncertain significance for condition'
      relationships (GENO:0000840, GENO:0000843, GENO:0000845).

    name: object
    annotations:
      requirements:
        tag: requirements
        value: RCS.STRUCTURED_STATEMENT
    description: The definition text.
    comments:
    - The object of a Statement can be any Entity or concept that is related to the
      subject, e.g. for Genetic Variation subjects the object is often a disease,
      drug, gene, molecular consequence, functional impact on gene or protein.

    owner: DefinitionStatement

    - Proposition

    required: true
